### 9.S Source-preserved detail — Layers 0–1
###### Global record candidates relevant to Layers 0–1

| Candidate | Owner | Relevance to Layers 0–1 | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `DatasetRecord` | Layer 1 | Public dataset identity, source, subject/session/run metadata, protocol scope. | final_registry_entry |
| `WindowRecord` | Layer 1 | Window/trial segmentation and split membership consumed by Layers 2–10. | final_registry_entry |
| `TrialRecord` | unresolved / possible Layer 1 | Architecture refers to trial-level records and trial metadata, but the system-wide canonical table and Layer 1 schema expose `trial_id`/`parent_trial_id` inside `WindowRecord` rather than defining a separate `TrialRecord`. | `inferred_candidate`; `requires_confirmation: true`; not promoted in this audited section |
| `SplitRecord` | Layer 1 | Train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation memberships and leakage controls. | final_registry_entry |
| `PreprocessingRecord` | Layer 1 | Preprocessing configuration and fit-scope lineage. | final_registry_entry |
| `LabelMapRecord` | Layer 1 | Original-to-normalized label mapping and proxy-intent note. | final_registry_entry |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` | Layer 1 | Artifact/channel/window quality flags. | final_registry_entry |
| `ValidationReport` | Layer 1 / validation infrastructure | Schema, leakage, metadata, split, and completeness validation. | final_registry_entry |
| `Layer1Manifest` | Layer 1 | Canonical bundle manifest for Layer 1 records, configs, cards, reports, and readiness status. | final_registry_entry |
| `DatasetCard` | Layer 1 produces; Layer 10 displays/exports | Human-facing dataset provenance, limitations, and protocol notes. | final_registry_entry |
| `ProtocolCard` | Layer 1 produces; Layer 10 displays/exports | Human-facing protocol, split, budget, window, and leakage notes. | final_registry_entry |
| `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | Layer 1 | Evaluation-readiness artifact for downstream ablation scripts and dashboard. | final_registry_entry |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` | Layer 0 / final-evidence governance | Links claims to records, metrics, limitations, ablations, cards, and final evidence. | normalized_candidate; requires confirmation of exact schema |
| `ClaimLedger` | Layer 0 | Ledger of allowed/prohibited claims and limitation wording. | normalized_candidate; architecture names “claim ledger” but not full schema |
| `InvalidClaimFlag` | Layer 0 | Claim-safety warning/failure marker. | normalized_candidate |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Layer 0 / evaluation governance | Downgrades incomplete or unsupported evidence. | final_registry_entry as evaluation/claim-safety artifact |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Evaluation / Layer 0 claim governance | Preserves negative results and prevents silent omission. | final_registry_entry as evaluation/claim-safety artifact |

###### 8. Canonical Record Entries

###### 8.1 `DatasetRecord`

| Field | Registry value |
|---|---|
| Record category | canonical public-data source record |
| Owning layer | Layer 1 |
| Producer module | Dataset registry manager; metadata normalizer |
| Consumer layers | Layers 2–10 and Layer 0 |
| Consumer modules | Decoder modules, calibration, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, policy modules, StressForge, embodiment demo, dashboard, claim-safety gate |
| Created in implementation phase | Phase 1 |
| Validated in implementation phase | Phase 1 |
| Consumed starting in phase | Phase 2 |
| Used in ablation step(s) | A0–A13 as source identity/matched-key metadata |
| Used in dashboard/card | Dataset card, dashboard source summary, reproducibility package |
| Used in paper/thesis claim | Public-data and low-calibration protocol claims only |
| Required source records | Public EEG dataset source and metadata |
| Required fields | `dataset_id`, `dataset_name`, `source_name`, `source_version`, `license_note`, `subject_id`, `original_subject_id`, `session_id`, `run_id`, `task_set`, `channel_names_original`, `channel_names_selected`, `sampling_rate_original`, `sampling_rate_target`, `preprocessing_id`, `split_id`, `protocol_version`, `claim_scope_tag` |
| Optional fields | Dataset-specific notes, mirror/cache path, artifact-note availability if explicitly recorded |
| Controlled vocabulary fields | dataset status, task family, claim-scope tag, validation status |
| Universal lineage-envelope classification | required_global: `record_id`, `dataset_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `producer_layer`, `validation_status`, `phase_id`, `layer_id`, `created_timestamp`, `claim_boundary_tags`; required_if_applicable: `subject_id`, `session_id`, `run_id`, `split_id`, `preprocessing_id`, `config_hash`, `seed`, `source_artifact_ids`; record_specific: `source_name`, `source_version`, `license_note`; forbidden: policy IDs, reward/cost IDs, stress IDs, embodiment IDs unless used only as downstream source references |
| Validation rules | Schema valid; public source documented; metadata complete enough for protocol; source version/license note present; claim scope tag present |
| Split/leakage constraints | Must not allow subject/session/run leakage contrary to split protocol |
| Simulation/proxy/clinical boundary | Public EEG only; not clinical BCI-FES validation |
| Failure modes | Missing source, incomplete metadata, license ambiguity, split mismatch, claim-scope tag missing |
| Missingness interpretation | Dataset excluded, optional-only, or diagnostic-only depending on status |
| Canonical name | `DatasetRecord` |
| Allowed internal aliases | `dataset_record`, `dataset_meta` if exported as `DatasetRecord` |
| Display aliases | “Dataset record”, “Public dataset record” |
| Deprecated aliases | none confirmed |
| Forbidden aliases | “ClinicalDatasetRecord”, “PatientSafetyDatasetRecord” |
| Repository location | `records/dataset_records/` |
| Lifecycle stage | validated/promoted_to_canonical after Phase 1 validation |
| Schema maturity | draft_schema until implemented and validated; target `validated_schema` / `thesis_ready_schema` |
| Branch status | core |
| Promotion rule | Promote only after schema, source, lineage, and split-link validation |
| Canonicalization rule | Export uses canonical fields and protocol version |
| Diagnostic-only condition | Missing validation, missing split ID, incomplete provenance, unresolved license/source |
| Thesis-ready condition | Validated schema, lineage, source version, split linkage, cards/manifests, claim tags |
| Clean source-record status | clean source record |
| Derived-record status | not derived |
| Allowed derivations | DatasetCard, Layer1Manifest, dashboard summaries, evaluation-readiness artifact |
| Forbidden mutations | Stress, simulation, policy adaptation, dashboard filtering, manual repair, or threshold tuning overwriting the validated record |

| `HighConfidenceWrongTable` | `evaluation_artifact` | L3 error miner | L10, L4/L6 offline analysis, thesis negative results | Prediction/calibration/uncertainty records, eval labels | Confident wrong predictions, source IDs, class-pair errors, grouping keys, confidence threshold, correctness source, diagnostic status | Source records, evaluation split IDs, threshold/config, metric dictionary if summarized | Derived evaluation-only artifact | diagnostic_only | dashboard warning/table input | A1–A3 | Cannot be decision-time feature; limitation evidence only |
| `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` | `metric_artifact` / dashboard-readable candidate | L3 dashboard/card exporter | L10 backend/cards/figures/manifests | Layer 3 records/reports, metric dictionary | Plot-ready metrics, bin tables, risk-coverage curves, filters, warning flags, card refs, source-record IDs, export lineage | Source records, metric dictionary IDs, filter config, export config, seed/hash | Derived dashboard input record | normalized_candidate; schema unresolved with L10 | required dashboard input; not dashboard output | A1–A3 dashboard evidence | Inherits source limitations; not primary evidence |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` | `evaluation_artifact` | L3 selective/threshold modules | Evaluation scripts, L10, final demonstration, thesis | Calibration/selective/threshold records, metric dictionary | Matched-coverage/cost points, A1–A3 keys, threshold sufficiency/calibration failure notes, high-confidence wrong summaries, diagnostic flags | Matched keys, metric dictionary, source record IDs, config/seed | Derived evaluation artifact | final if matched keys complete | required dashboard input | A1–A3 | Fair comparison support; unmatched comparisons diagnostic |

###### 8.2 Aliases and forbidden lineage fields

- Allowed internal aliases: `predictions`, `raw_predictions`, `decoder_outputs`, `calibrated_predictions`, `uncertainty_features`, `threshold_registry`, `selective_baseline`, only when mapped before export.
- Forbidden exported aliases: `y_true`, `y_pred`, `prob_vector` as final field names. They must map to `label_true`, `predicted_class`, and `probability_vector`.
- Forbidden lineage/fields in decision-time records: future reward, future correctness, clinical outcome, embodiment outcome, safety approval, post-hoc high-confidence wrong flags, test-derived threshold status unless explicitly oracle/diagnostic.

### 9.S Source-preserved detail — Layers 4–5
###### 3.1 Global record candidates relevant to Layers 4-5

| Record family | Producer / owner | Layer 4-5 relevance | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DatasetRecord, WindowRecord, SplitRecord, PreprocessingRecord, LabelMapRecord, ArtifactFlagRecord | Layer 1 | Provide public-data, split, window, channel/artifact, label, and claim-scope lineage. Layer 4 consumes Window/ArtifactFlag context; Layer 5 consumes Window/artifact/subject-session identity. | canonical_entry |
| PredictionRecord, ModelRegistryRecord, SubjectProfileRecord, EnsembleControlRecord, FailureCaseIndex | Layer 2 | PredictionRecord is a primary input for both layers; Model/subject/ensemble/failure artifacts support agreement, temporal trust, A0/A4 baselines, and failure analysis. | canonical_entry |
| CalibrationRecord, UncertaintyRecord, SelectivePredictionRecord, ThresholdRegistryRecord, Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable | Layer 3 | Layer 4 uses calibration/uncertainty/thresholds to make IHARQ decisions; Layer 5 uses trajectories and selective-prediction diagnostics. | canonical_entry |
| EvidenceQualityRecord, IHARQDecisionRecord, CombinedEvidenceRecord, FallbackDecisionRecord, UnsafeEventRecord, IHARQAblationRecord, IHARQTraceRecord | Layer 4, with EvidenceQualityRecord also produced by Layer 6 when learned quality is enabled | Core Layer 4 output family; Layer 5 consumes IHARQ decisions and evidence-quality histories. | canonical_entry with shared-producer note for EvidenceQualityRecord |
| RegimeStateRecord, TrustStateRecord, regime_timelines.csv, trust_scores.csv, stop_loss_warnings.csv | Layer 5 | Core Layer 5 output family; Layer 4 consumes RegimeRisk feedback; Layers 6/7/9/10 consume temporal trust context. | canonical_entry |
| ReadinessContextRecord, PolicyActionRecord, DeferralRecord, PolicyUpdateTrace | Layer 6 / Layer 6-7 policy-update branch | Downstream consumers of Layer 4-5 records; relevant to leakage, policy-update separation, and dashboard filtering. | external_to_scope but cross-layer relevant |
| TransitionRecord, SafetyEventRecord, StressProfileRecord, EmbodimentStateRecord, EmbodimentOutcomeRecord | Layers 7-9 | Simulation/stress/embodiment records may contextualize Layer 4-5 evaluation but remain simulation/proxy-only. | external_to_scope, optional/stretch |
| EvaluationOutcomeRecord, MetricDictionaryEntry, MatchedComparisonReport, NegativeResultNote, ClaimEvidenceMatrix, DashboardMetricRecord, DashboardViewRecord, CardRecord, ReproducibilityManifest | Evaluation scripts / Layer 10 / Layer 0 where applicable | Required to make Layer 4-5 results thesis-ready, dashboard-visible, reproducible, and claim-bounded. | canonical/evaluation_artifact families |

###### 8. Canonical Record Entries

The entries below use the framework ontology. Unless otherwise stated, the universal lineage envelope is governed as follows:

- **Required global lineage fields:** identity field (`record_id`, `artifact_id`, or report ID), `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `producer_layer`, `layer_id`, `module_id`, `validation_status`, `lifecycle_stage`, `claim_boundary_tags`, and `limitation_tags`.
- **Required-if-applicable lineage fields:** `run_id`, `experiment_id`, `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `time_index`, `split_id`, `model_id`, `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `evidence_quality_id`, `iharq_decision_id`, `regime_state_id`, `policy_id`, `transition_id`, `episode_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `dashboard_export_id`, `card_id`, `figure_id`, `table_id`, `claim_id`, `phase_id`, `ablation_id`, `sub_ablation_id`, `metric_dictionary_id`, `matched_comparison_key`, `negative_result_note_id`, `source_record_ids`, `config_hash`, `seed`, and `created_timestamp`. `source_record_ids` are mandatory for derived, stress-conditioned, simulation-conditioned, dashboard-generated, evaluation-derived, or claim-evidence artifacts, but not forced into clean source records where the architecture does not require them.
- **Forbidden lineage fields:** future labels, future rewards, future outcomes, or oracle correctness fields inside decision-time records unless explicitly partitioned as evaluation-only and excluded from decision-time use.

###### 8.1 Layer 4 canonical and candidate record entries


###### IHARQDecisionRecord

- **Record category:** canonical_record.
- **Owning layer:** Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification. For `EvidenceQualityRecord`, merge reconciliation must preserve that Layer 4 produces the rule-derived version while Layer 6 may produce a learned version when enabled.
- **Producer module:** Layer 4 — IHARQ rule engine / decision logger.
- **Consumer layers/modules:** Layers 6, 7, 9, 10; evaluation scripts.
- **Created in implementation phase:** Phase 4, except shared or downstream-learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants that may also be created in Phase 6.
- **Validated in implementation phase:** Phase 4 validation gate; dashboard/export validation Phase 14; final thesis evidence Phase 15.
- **Consumed starting in phase:** Phase 5 for IHARQ histories consumed by RegimeRisk; Phase 6 for policy context; Phase 8 for simulation; Phase 12/13 for optional embodiment through simulation-compatible gating; Phase 14 for dashboard.
- **Ablation use:** A5 primary; A6/A7 participation; A0-A4 are baselines/controls, not owners.
- **Dashboard/card use:** IHARQ timeline, evidence-flow view, reason-code distribution, request/combine view, fallback view, unsafe-event view, baseline comparison view, ablation view, matched-comparison view, stress-conditioned IHARQ view, trace-completeness view, IHARQ reliability card, claim-evidence coverage view.
- **Paper/thesis claim:** computational evidence-verification and proxy readiness-control claim only; no clinical safety, patient-safety, real rehabilitation, medical-device, or real muscle stimulation claim.
- **Required source records:** PredictionRecord, CalibrationRecord where calibrated mode is used, UncertaintyRecord, WindowRecord/WindowHistoryRecord where temporal logic is used, ArtifactFlagRecord where signal/channel safety is inspected, ThresholdRegistryRecord, optional RegimeStateRecord, optional model/channel/agreement helper views, and evaluation artifacts only after decision.
- **Required fields:** final action token, accepted class, fallback/unsafe/uncertain flags, request count, combined summary, action cost, reason code, rule path, ablation IDs, matched key, metric dictionary, claim boundary.
- **Optional fields:** stress context, embodiment compatibility, simulation outcome/evaluation outcome, trust weights, conformal proxies, negative-result note IDs, dashboard export IDs, local ablation IDs, diagnostic flags, and branch-specific fields when applicable.
- **Controlled vocabulary fields:** IHARQ action tokens, reason-code categories, validation status, evaluation mode, ablation ID, claim-boundary tags, DiagnosticOnlyFlag, fallback routes, unsafe trigger classes.
- **Lineage envelope class:** source-derived decision/evaluation record.
- **Required global lineage fields:** as listed at the start of Section 8; `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `iharq_decision_id` where applicable, `metric_dictionary_id`, `matched_comparison_key` for evaluation rows.
- **Required-if-applicable lineage fields:** `regime_state_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `transition_id`, `policy_id`, `dashboard_export_id`, `claim_id`.
- **Forbidden lineage fields:** decision-time use of true label, future correctness, future reward, future stress outcome, or hidden dashboard-derived metric.
- **Validation rules:** schema validity; source-record join validity; split/leakage check; action-token validation; reason-code presence; threshold registry legality; matched-comparison completeness for evaluation; dashboard trace completeness for thesis export.
- **Split/leakage constraints:** threshold/calibration/IHARQ rule tuning must not use held-out test outcomes; evaluation labels are post-decision only.
- **Simulation/proxy/clinical boundary:** public EEG and simulated/proxy readiness only. Unsafe/fallback/stop language is computational or simulation-bounded.
- **Failure modes:** missing reason code, missing source record, invalid probability vector, ID mismatch, unregistered threshold, hidden fallback, unsafe overclaim, unmatched comparison, dashboard-only metric, negative result omitted.
- **Missingness interpretation:** missing required fields block thesis-ready output or trigger explicit degraded/diagnostic mode. Optional missingness must be represented, not assumed clean.
- **Canonical name:** `IHARQDecisionRecord`.
- **Allowed internal aliases:** implementation-local snake_case filenames or table names only if exported to the canonical name.
- **Display aliases:** human-readable dashboard labels such as IHARQ decision, fallback log, unsafe-event table, evidence quality, IHARQ trace, or IHARQ ablation table.
- **Deprecated aliases:** none explicitly defined in the architecture.
- **Forbidden aliases:** aliases that rewrite Layer 4 stored action tokens, treat no-action as a Layer 4 canonical action token, call unsafe a clinical safety decision, or rename ordinary ensemble voting as IHARQ.
- **Repository location:** see Section 17; canonical homes include `records/iharq_records/`, `records/evidence_quality_records/`, `records/evaluation_outcome_records/layer4_iharq/`, with run-local exports under Layer 4 results where configured.
- **Lifecycle stage:** planned/draft_schema until implemented; promoted_to_canonical only after validation and run provenance.
- **Schema maturity:** draft_schema from architecture; thesis_ready_schema only after implementation validators pass.
- **Branch status:** core/target for A5 IHARQ-lite; stretch/simulation-only/proxy-only when stress or embodiment context is used.
- **Promotion rule:** promote from run-specific record to canonical family only if schema, lineage, config hash, seed, source-record IDs, validation status, and claim tags are complete.
- **Diagnostic-only condition:** unmatched comparison, missing metric dictionary, missing trace, missing source IDs, evaluation leakage, missing negative-result note, or missing dashboard/export lineage.
- **Thesis-ready condition:** valid source records, legal thresholds, complete reason/action trace, matched comparisons where claims compare variants, metric dictionary, negative-result visibility, dashboard/card/export lineage, claim-evidence entry, Layer 0 limitations.
- **Clean source-record status:** not a clean upstream source record; derived-from-clean-source-records but canonical Layer 4 output family.
- **Allowed derivations:** dashboard metrics, cards, figures, tables, evaluation summaries, stress-conditioned copies, matched-comparison reports, claim-evidence entries.
- **Forbidden mutations:** rewriting source Prediction/Calibration/Uncertainty/Window records, retuning thresholds post hoc, changing stored action tokens, adding evaluation labels to decision-time records, overwriting clean records with stress/simulation/dashboard edits.
- **Source claim-boundary tags:** public_eeg_only, proxy_readiness, computational_evidence_verification, not_clinical_validation. Add simulation_only, stress_conditioned, embodiment_proxy_only, or diagnostic_only when applicable.
- **Strictest claim boundary:** computational/proxy evidence-verification; never clinical safety.
- **Example minimal instance:** not provided for this registry entry because the architecture gives field requirements but not enough concrete valid row values without inventing IDs, except for Layer 5 RegimeStateRecord where an illustrative example appears in the source architecture.

###### RegimeStateRecord

- **Record category:** canonical_record / derived_record.
- **Owning layer:** Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring.

- **Dashboard/card use:** regime timeline, trust allocation, stop-loss view, risk explanation, stress-regime view, embodiment-risk view, ablation comparison, RegimeCard, trust-state plots, temporal-failure audits.
- **Paper/thesis claim:** temporal trust proxy, temporal unreliability, static-threshold limitation, regime-aware decision comparison, and interpretability claims only. No clinical fatigue or neurological-state diagnosis.
- **Required source records:** WindowRecord, PredictionRecord, CalibrationRecord when available, UncertaintyRecord, EvidenceQualityRecord where available, IHARQDecisionRecord where available, optional StressProfileRecord, TransitionRecord, EmbodimentState/Outcome records only in declared simulation/proxy mode, SubjectProfileRecord as auxiliary context.

- **Optional fields:** stress_profile_id, embodiment_state_id, transition_id, policy_action_id, calibration_drift_score, channel_dropout_score, model_family_shift_score, drift/fatigue/dropout flags, recovery status, evaluation_label, negative-control IDs, dashboard export IDs.
- **Controlled vocabulary fields:** regime labels, risk bands, risk trend, trust target type, trust band, update source, stop-loss status, recommendation, reason codes, claim-boundary tags, DiagnosticOnlyFlags.
- **Lineage envelope class:** temporal derived record or evaluation artifact.
- **Required global lineage fields:** as listed at the start of Section 8; temporal location and source-record IDs are mandatory.
- **Required-if-applicable lineage fields:** `iharq_decision_id`, `evidence_quality_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `transition_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `policy_id`, `dashboard_export_id`, `card_id`, `claim_id`, `ablation_id`, `metric_dictionary_id`, `matched_comparison_key`.
- **Forbidden lineage fields:** non-causal future information in decision-time regime estimation; clinical fatigue labels unless explicitly public and claim-safe; hidden dashboard-edited state.
- **Validation rules:** temporal ordering; causal cutoff; split isolation; finite scores; aligned IDs; simulation/proxy tags; optional trust-state linkage; stop-loss trigger trace; negative-control/matched-comparison completeness for A7 claims.
- **Split/leakage constraints:** rolling windows must not cross forbidden split boundaries or read future labels/outcomes; correctness/outcomes are evaluation-only unless legally past in a declared online/simulation protocol.
- **Simulation/proxy/clinical boundary:** drift, fatigue-like, dropout-risk, and unsafe labels are proxy operating-state labels; stress/embodiment contexts are simulation/proxy-only.
- **Failure modes:** future-information leakage, non-causal features, proxy labels overclaimed as physiological diagnoses, unstable labels, stop-loss untested, trust scores not used or untraceable, missing negative controls, unmatched regime-aware comparison.
- **Missingness interpretation:** missing temporal ordering blocks Layer 5; missing IHARQ history weakens decision-relevance; missing trust-state rows only matters when independent trust timelines are consumed; missing negative controls blocks A7 improvement claim.
- **Canonical name:** `RegimeStateRecord`.
- **Allowed internal aliases:** implementation-local names such as `regime_risk`, `regime_timeline`, `trust_scores`, or `stop_loss_log` only when mapped to canonical exports.

- **Deprecated aliases:** none explicitly defined.
- **Forbidden aliases:** clinical fatigue detector, neurological state detector, patient-risk monitor, medical safety controller, or any name that removes proxy/non-clinical limitations.

- **Schema maturity:** draft_schema from architecture; thesis_ready_schema only after implementation validation, negative controls, dashboard lineage, and claim-evidence linkage.
- **Branch status:** target/stretch for RegimeRisk; simulation_only/proxy_only for stress/embodiment-derived fields; optional/future_work for sequence-model regime estimator.
- **Promotion rule:** promote only if causal temporal features, source IDs, configs, thresholds, reason codes, validation status, and claim tags are complete.
- **Diagnostic-only condition:** temporal leakage, missing source IDs, missing A7 matched comparison, missing shuffled/random negative control when claimed, missing metric dictionary, or absent limitation tags.
- **Thesis-ready condition:** valid causal timeline, matched regime-aware/unaware comparison where improvement is claimed, metric dictionary, negative-control report, negative-result note visibility, RegimeCard/dashboard lineage, claim-evidence entry, Layer 0 limitations.
- **Clean source-record status:** derived from clean source records; not allowed to overwrite public-data, prediction, calibration, uncertainty, or IHARQ source records.
- **Allowed derivations:** regime timelines, trust plots, stop-loss summaries, dashboard metrics, RegimeCards, matched-comparison reports, stress/embodiment diagnostic summaries, claim-evidence entries.
- **Forbidden mutations:** rewriting upstream records, post-hoc tuning on test outcomes, using future outcomes, treating stress/embodiment proxy outcomes as clinical observations, dashboard edits to regime state.

- **Required fields:** dataset/subject/session/horizon, regime config, trust config, stop-loss setting, ablation or negative-control ID, matched key, metric dictionary, source regime/trust records, diagnostic flag, negative-result note.
- **Optional fields:** stress_profile_id, embodiment_state_id, transition_id, policy_action_id, calibration_drift_score, channel_dropout_score, model_family_shift_score, drift/fatigue/dropout flags, recovery status, evaluation_label, negative-control IDs, dashboard export IDs.
- **Controlled vocabulary fields:** regime labels, risk bands, risk trend, trust target type, trust band, update source, stop-loss status, recommendation, reason codes, claim-boundary tags, DiagnosticOnlyFlags.
- **Lineage envelope class:** temporal derived record or evaluation artifact.
- **Required global lineage fields:** as listed at the start of Section 8; temporal location and source-record IDs are mandatory.
- **Required-if-applicable lineage fields:** `iharq_decision_id`, `evidence_quality_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `transition_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `policy_id`, `dashboard_export_id`, `card_id`, `claim_id`, `ablation_id`, `metric_dictionary_id`, `matched_comparison_key`.
- **Forbidden lineage fields:** non-causal future information in decision-time regime estimation; clinical fatigue labels unless explicitly public and claim-safe; hidden dashboard-edited state.
- **Validation rules:** temporal ordering; causal cutoff; split isolation; finite scores; aligned IDs; simulation/proxy tags; optional trust-state linkage; stop-loss trigger trace; negative-control/matched-comparison completeness for A7 claims.
- **Split/leakage constraints:** rolling windows must not cross forbidden split boundaries or read future labels/outcomes; correctness/outcomes are evaluation-only unless legally past in a declared online/simulation protocol.
- **Simulation/proxy/clinical boundary:** drift, fatigue-like, dropout-risk, and unsafe labels are proxy operating-state labels; stress/embodiment contexts are simulation/proxy-only.
- **Failure modes:** future-information leakage, non-causal features, proxy labels overclaimed as physiological diagnoses, unstable labels, stop-loss untested, trust scores not used or untraceable, missing negative controls, unmatched regime-aware comparison.
- **Missingness interpretation:** missing temporal ordering blocks Layer 5; missing IHARQ history weakens decision-relevance; missing trust-state rows only matters when independent trust timelines are consumed; missing negative controls blocks A7 improvement claim.
- **Canonical name:** `Layer 5 EvaluationOutcomeRecord`.
- **Allowed internal aliases:** implementation-local names such as `regime_risk`, `regime_timeline`, `trust_scores`, or `stop_loss_log` only when mapped to canonical exports.
- **Display aliases:** RegimeRisk state, temporal trust state, trust timeline, stop-loss warnings, RegimeRisk card.
- **Deprecated aliases:** none explicitly defined.
- **Forbidden aliases:** clinical fatigue detector, neurological state detector, patient-risk monitor, medical safety controller, or any name that removes proxy/non-clinical limitations.
- **Repository location:** see Section 17; canonical homes include `records/regime_state_records/`, `records/trust_state_records/`, `records/evaluation_outcome_records/layer5_regimerisk/`, with timeline/trust/stop-loss artifacts linked through manifests and cards.
- **Lifecycle stage:** planned/draft_schema until implemented; promoted_to_canonical only after validation.
- **Schema maturity:** draft_schema from architecture; thesis_ready_schema only after implementation validation, negative controls, dashboard lineage, and claim-evidence linkage.
- **Branch status:** target/stretch for RegimeRisk; simulation_only/proxy_only for stress/embodiment-derived fields; optional/future_work for sequence-model regime estimator.
- **Promotion rule:** promote only if causal temporal features, source IDs, configs, thresholds, reason codes, validation status, and claim tags are complete.
- **Diagnostic-only condition:** temporal leakage, missing source IDs, missing A7 matched comparison, missing shuffled/random negative control when claimed, missing metric dictionary, or absent limitation tags.
- **Thesis-ready condition:** valid causal timeline, matched regime-aware/unaware comparison where improvement is claimed, metric dictionary, negative-control report, negative-result note visibility, RegimeCard/dashboard lineage, claim-evidence entry, Layer 0 limitations.
- **Clean source-record status:** derived from clean source records; not allowed to overwrite public-data, prediction, calibration, uncertainty, or IHARQ source records.
- **Allowed derivations:** regime timelines, trust plots, stop-loss summaries, dashboard metrics, RegimeCards, matched-comparison reports, stress/embodiment diagnostic summaries, claim-evidence entries.
- **Forbidden mutations:** rewriting upstream records, post-hoc tuning on test outcomes, using future outcomes, treating stress/embodiment proxy outcomes as clinical observations, dashboard edits to regime state.
- **Source claim-boundary tags:** public_eeg_only, temporal_trust_proxy, proxy_readiness, not_clinical_validation, not_real_patient_safety; add simulation_only/stress_conditioned/embodiment_proxy_only when used.
- **Strictest claim boundary:** temporal trust proxy; no medical fatigue/health-state diagnosis.
- **Example minimal instance:** No concrete minimal instance is included because valid IDs/values would need to be invented.

###### 8.1 Audited universal lineage-envelope classification by record family

This addendum repairs the main structural weakness of the previous draft: it used a shared lineage description but did not explicitly classify lineage fields for each canonical record family.

| Canonical record | Lineage envelope class | Required global lineage fields | Required-if-applicable lineage fields | Record-specific lineage fields | Forbidden lineage fields | Source-record preservation rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ReadinessContextRecord` | derived decision-time policy context | `record_id`, `run_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_layer`, `producer_module`, `validation_status`, `lifecycle_stage`, `config_hash`, `claim_boundary_tags`, `source_record_ids` | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `model_id`, `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `evidence_quality_id`, `iharq_decision_id`, `regime_state_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `policy_id`, `phase_id`, `ablation_id`, `seed` | `action_space_version`, `decision_time_cutoff`, `observable_field_set_id`, `target_partition_id` | `true_label`, `decoder_correct`, `future_reward`, `future_window_features`, `future_embodiment_outcome`, `oracle_costs` as ordinary policy-visible fields | Preserve all upstream clean source IDs; create new version for stress/simulation/embodiment variants. |
| `EvidenceQualityRecord` | derived evidence-quality/proxy reliability record | `record_id`, `run_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_layer`, `producer_module`, `validation_status`, `config_hash`, `claim_boundary_tags`, `source_record_ids` | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `model_id`, `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `phase_id`, `ablation_id`, `seed` | `evidence_quality_id`, `target_construction_id`, `evidence_source_ids`, `proxy_target_status` | decision-time `true_label` or correctness target as visible feature | Derived from prediction/calibration/uncertainty/stability sources; targets must remain partitioned. |
| `PolicyActionRecord` | policy-output canonical record | `record_id`, `run_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_layer`, `producer_module`, `validation_status`, `config_hash`, `policy_id`, `claim_boundary_tags`, `source_record_ids` | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `iharq_decision_id`, `regime_state_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `phase_id`, `ablation_id`, `seed` | `policy_action_id`, `action_space_version`, `legality_mask_id`, `policy_family`, `action_origin`, `frozen_or_update_mode` | hidden label, future reward, future transition, oracle action as production action unless explicitly diagnostic/evaluation-only | Preserve context and source IHARQ tokens; never overwrite upstream decisions. |
| `DeferralRecord` | policy-routing derived record | `record_id`, `run_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_layer`, `producer_module`, `validation_status`, `config_hash`, `claim_boundary_tags`, `source_record_ids` | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `policy_id`, `phase_id`, `ablation_id`, `seed` | `deferral_record_id`, `deferral_target`, `deferral_reason`, `fallback_source_id`, `fallback_cost_config_id`, `matched_group_id` | real expert label unless explicitly available and licensed; oracle fallback as decision-time feature | Preserve policy/context records; fallback proxies must be versioned and labeled. |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` | trace artifact for update governance | `artifact_id` or `record_id`, `run_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_layer`, `producer_module`, `validation_status`, `config_hash`, `policy_id`, `claim_boundary_tags` | `transition_id`, `policy_action_id`, `policy_update_trace_id`, `episode_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `phase_id`, `ablation_id`, `seed`, `source_record_ids` | `update_mode`, `update_step`, `reward_config_id`, `cost_config_id`, `legality_mask_id`, `training_adaptation_split`, `held_out_evaluation_split`, `disabled_update_audit_status` | any claim of real online deployment adaptation | One trace per mutation; disabled-update audit where configured; no mutation of frozen records. |

The final registry merge should consolidate layer-specific `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, and `ClaimEvidenceManifest` instances under global evaluation artifact families with layer-specific contexts rather than creating incompatible layer-owned semantic families.

## 10. Interface Contract Registry

### 10.1 Interface organization
Interfaces are organized by source-defined interface type: record, module, adapter, dashboard, policy, simulation, embodiment, validation, claim-safety, repository, and related handoff families. Producer side, consumer side, payload, required/optional fields, allowed states/actions, validation/error/retry behavior, feedback permission, dashboard visibility, and claim-safety relevance are retained from the source entries.

###### Global interface families

- Record interfaces from Layer 1 to Layers 2–10.
- Claim-safety interfaces from Layer 0 to all layers and final thesis artifacts.
- Validation interfaces from Layer 1 validation/audit modules to downstream consumers.
- Dashboard interfaces from saved records/evaluation artifacts into Layer 10.
- Repository interfaces from configs, records, reports, cards, and manifests into reproducibility packages.
- Evaluation interfaces connecting Layer 1 source identities and split keys to A0–A13 comparisons.

- Record interfaces from Layers 1-3 into IHARQ and RegimeRisk.
- IHARQ decision/evidence interfaces from Layer 4 to Layers 5-10.

- RegimeRisk context interface from Layer 5 to Layer 6 policy contexts.

- Claim-safety interfaces from records/cards/figures/tables to Layer 0 claim review.

###### 9.1 Interface allowed-states and allowed-actions supplement

This audit adds the explicit allowed-state and allowed-action layer required by the framework without changing otherwise valid interface ownership.

| Interface | Allowed states | Allowed actions | Forbidden actions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L2-L3-to-L4 Evidence Input Interface | valid, degraded, missing_required, leakage_blocked, diagnostic_only | validate, read, reject, downgrade, request rerun | mutate upstream records, tune thresholds on evaluation outcomes |
| Layer 4 IHARQ Decision Interface | accept, wait, request_evidence, combine_evidence, fallback, uncertain, unsafe | export decision, link evidence/fallback/unsafe records, expose dashboard-readable trace | rename stored tokens, reinterpret as clinical approval |
| Layer 4 Combined Evidence Interface | eligible, ineligible, contradiction_detected, combined, rejected | combine declared sources, reject invalid combinations, link source windows | hide contradiction, overwrite source windows |
| Layer 4 Fallback/Unsafe Interface | fallback_available, fallback_unavailable, unsafe_triggered, unsafe_cleared, diagnostic_only | route fallback, block unsafe action, log warning, expose dashboard warning | treat unsafe event as real patient-safety validation |
| Layer 5-to-L4 RegimeRisk Feedback Interface | regime_unaware, regime_aware, stop_loss_warning, stop_loss_active, unsafe_recommendation, diagnostic_only | tighten within declared bounds, request stricter evidence, restrict trusted set, recommend fallback/no_action/unsafe, log original-versus-adjusted decision | hidden override, future-label feedback, unlogged threshold mutation |
| Layer 5-to-L6 Policy Context Interface | valid_context, protected_fields_removed, stop_loss_active, unsafe_context, diagnostic_only | assemble policy context, constrain legality/action space, pass update governance to Layer 6/7 | expose evaluation-only future outcome fields to policy |
| Layer 5-to-L7 Simulation State Interface | clean_simulation, stress_conditioned, stop_loss_active, unsafe_simulated_state, diagnostic_only | inject regime state into simulation, preserve simulation-only tags | convert simulation result into real deployment claim |
| Layer 5-to-L9 Embodiment Gate Interface | allow, strong_evidence_only, conservative_command, no_action, safe_hold, unsafe_block, diagnostic_only | gate simulated/proxy embodiment commands, log command-gating reason | claim real muscle stimulation or clinical control |
| Layer 4/5-to-L10 Dashboard Interface | readable, incomplete, warning_required, export_blocked, exported | read, validate, filter, summarize, visualize, warn, export, package | recompute decisions, retune thresholds, repair missing records, create hidden primary evidence |
| Claim-Safety Interface | pending_review, approved_with_limits, downgraded, blocked, diagnostic_only | attach limitations, downgrade claims, block overclaims, require paper/dashboard warning | remove inherited limitations |
| Repository Promotion Interface | run_specific, validated, promoted_to_canonical, superseded, deprecated, thesis_ready | promote with lineage, retain source run, supersede with repair log | overwrite validated clean source records |

###### 3.3 Global interface families

- Policy-context record interface from Layers 2–5 to Layer 6.
- Layer 6 policy-action and deferral handoff to Layer 7 and optional Layer 9 paths.
- Layer 7 state/action/transition/reward interface.
- Policy-update interface for contextual bandit and RL, with `PolicyUpdateTrace` and disabled-update audit separation.
- Layer 8 stress interface through `StressProfileRecord` and `StressScheduleRecord`.
- Layer 9 embodiment gateway interface through response identifiers and Layer 9-owned records.
- Layer 10 dashboard read-only interface.
- Layer 0 claim-safety and limitation inheritance interface.

## 11. Vocabulary and Taxonomy Registry

### 11.1 Vocabulary governance
Vocabulary values are not invented or expanded beyond the source documents. Where aliases or naming risks are recorded, canonical names, allowed aliases, deprecated/forbidden aliases, dashboard display rules, and claim-safety effects remain governed by the source entries and the conflict ledger.

### 11.2 Source-preserved vocabularies, taxonomies, and alias ledgers

### 11.S Source-preserved detail — Layers 0–1

Downstream decision, policy, stress, simulation, embodiment, and dashboard vocabularies are referenced by Layer 0/1 for audit and lineage, but their semantic ownership remains with the producing layer or global evaluation/dashboard registry.

###### 10. Vocabulary and Taxonomy Registry


###### IHARQ action tokens (Layer 4)

- **Owner:** Layer 4.
- **Produced by:** Layer-owned rule/config/schema modules.
- **Consumed by:** downstream layers, evaluation scripts, Layer 10 dashboards/cards, and Layer 0 claim-safety checks where applicable.
- **Forbidden reinterpretations:** values must not be renamed or strengthened into unsupported clinical/safety/diagnostic meanings; display aliases must map back to canonical tokens.
- **Dashboard display rule:** display labels may be human-readable but must preserve canonical exported values.
- **Claim-safety effect:** values inherit proxy/computational/simulation limitations.


| Allowed value | Meaning / examples |
| --- | --- |
| accept | Use current predicted intent as ready for simulated action. |
| wait | Delay action without a targeted extra evidence source. |
| request_evidence | Acquire/evaluate another window, source, model-family prediction, channel check, signal check, or RegimeRisk update. |
| combine_evidence | Fuse current and previous windows/sources under eligibility rules. |
| fallback | Route to a safer/conservative alternative. |
| uncertain | State is undecidable but no explicit unsafe trigger is active. |
| unsafe | Block action and record a safety event. |

###### 10.1 Implementation-phase vocabulary
Allowed official phase IDs are exactly `Phase 0` through `Phase 15`. For this target scope, authoritative IDs are `Phase 0`, `Phase 4`, `Phase 5`, `Phase 6`, `Phase 8`, `Phase 9`, `Phase 12`, `Phase 13`, `Phase 14`, and `Phase 15` where relevant. Compressed waves or management groups are not authoritative phase IDs.

###### 10.2 Ablation-step vocabulary
Ablation IDs are evaluation-use metadata only. `A5` means IHARQ-lite, `A6` means IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator, and `A7` means IHARQ plus RegimeRisk. `A12` and `A13` may reference stress/embodiment use of Layer 4-5 outputs but do not own those outputs.

##### 4.4 Added vocabulary references

- IHARQ action-token values are explicitly bound to the Layer 4 canonical action vocabulary where consumed by Layers 6–7 or mapped to Layer 9: `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, `unsafe`.
- `combine` is preserved only as an unresolved alias candidate for `combine_evidence`; it is not a canonical export token.
- Policy-update modes are reinforced: `updates_disabled`, `frozen_policy_evaluation`, `simulation_training`, `simulation_adaptation`, `diagnostic_update_run`, `held_out_frozen_evaluation_after_training`, `forbidden_update_mode`.
- Stress categories are reinforced as evidence-side, simulation-side, policy-side, embodiment-response, dashboard-visualization, or diagnostic stress categories.
- Embodiment modes are reinforced as MyoSuite, OpenSim optional, and static replay where supported; no real-control interpretation is allowed.
- Exact reason-code, deferral-target, safety-severity, regime/trust-label, stress-family, and command-mapping vocabularies remain unresolved where the source documents do not enumerate final values.

### 12.1 Feedforward merge rule
Feedforward links retain source layer/module/output, target layer/module/input, purpose, transformation, validation before handoff, failure behavior, dashboard trace, and claim-safety tag. Links that are read-only, evaluation-only, simulation-only, or proxy-only retain those restrictions.

### 13.1 Feedback/loopback merge rule
Feedback entries distinguish read-only feedback, diagnostic feedback, simulation-authorized feedback, policy-update feedback, dashboard feedback, claim-safety feedback, and forbidden feedback. Training/adaptation permission, frozen-evaluation permission, `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit, simulation-only tags, and failure interpretation are preserved.

Layers 2–3 do **not** own update-capable policy behavior. If downstream Layers 6–7 use Layer 3 evidence in adaptive, bandit, or RL modes, policy-update governance belongs to those layers and requires `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit where applicable, frozen/update separation, and held-out evaluation separation.

## 14. Dashboard, Card, and Reproducibility Registry

### 14.1 Dashboard and reproducibility governance
Dashboard-readable source records remain separate from Layer 10 dashboard-generated outputs. Dashboard views, cards, figures, tables, warnings, exports, and manifests are traceable derived artifacts and do not become primary evidence unless source-record lineage, metric dictionary entries, configs, seeds, and manifests support the claim.

### 14.2 Source-preserved dashboard/card/reproducibility obligations

### 14.S Source-preserved detail — Layers 0–1

###### Global dashboard obligations

Layer 10 may read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, export, and package saved Layer 0–1 records and artifacts. Layer 10 must not silently create hidden primary evidence, fix split leakage, repair missing source records, suppress limitations, invent metric definitions, or overwrite Layer 1 clean source records.

###### 13. Dashboard, Card, and Reproducibility Obligations

| ClaimEvidenceMatrix | required_dashboard_input | claim_trace_view source/export | final claim-linkage artifact | yes |

###### Dashboard-generated outputs

Layer 10 may generate:

- Dashboard views that render Layer 1-produced `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard` content without replacing the source cards.
- Dataset and protocol summary panels derived from saved Layer 1 records, cards, validation reports, and manifests.
- Validation status panels.
- Leakage-audit warnings.
- Layer 1 manifest export panels.
- Ablation-readiness views.
- Claim-boundary warnings.
- Claim trace views.
- Reproducibility export manifests.
- Figure/table exports derived from registered source records and metric dictionary entries.

Layer 10 does **not** become the owner of `DatasetCard` or `ProtocolCard`; it may render, validate, summarize, and export them as read-only dashboard artifacts.

Layer 10 must not:

- Repair Layer 1 records.
- Recompute hidden evaluation evidence.
- Change split membership.
- Modify labels or preprocessing.
- Suppress public-data or non-clinical limitations.
- Promote dashboard views to primary evidence without traceable source records, metrics, configs, seeds, and manifests.

###### Required dashboard warnings

- Missing Layer 1 source record.
- Missing or failed `ValidationReport`.
- Missing `SplitRecord` or leakage failure.
- Missing claim-boundary tags.
- Missing metric dictionary entry for evaluation figures.
- Missing matched-comparison keys.
- Missing or stale manifest/config hash.
- Missing negative-result note where expected.
- Dashboard output not thesis-ready because lineage is incomplete.

###### 3.6 Global dashboard obligations

Layer 10 may read, validate, filter, summarize, visualize, warn, export, and package saved Layer 2/3 records. It must not retrain models, tune thresholds, recalibrate probabilities, create pseudo-labels, repair split leakage, rewrite source records, or produce hidden primary evidence. Cards, figures, tables, dashboard views, and exports are derived from saved records and must carry source-record IDs, metric dictionary references, config hashes, seeds, export manifest IDs, and inherited claim boundaries.

### 14.S Source-preserved detail — Layers 4–5
###### 3.7 Dashboard obligations
Layer 10 may read, validate, filter, summarize, visualize, warn, export, and package saved Layer 4-5 records. It must not recompute IHARQ decisions, retune thresholds, repair missing evidence, change ablation labels, generate hidden primary evidence, alter RegimeRisk histories, or remove claim-boundary limitations.

###### RegimeCard lineage

- **Record category:** card_artifact / manifest_artifact.
- **Owning layer:** Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring.
- **Producer module:** Layer 5 source lineage; Layer 10 renders/exports read-only.
- **Consumer layers/modules:** Layer 10, thesis appendix, reproducibility package.
- **Created in implementation phase:** Phase 5.
- **Validated in implementation phase:** Phase 5 validation gate; dashboard/export validation Phase 14; final thesis evidence Phase 15.
- **Consumed starting in phase:** Phase 4 feedback path when RegimeRisk-aware IHARQ is rerun; Phase 6 policy-context assembly; Phase 8 simulation; Phase 9 StressForge analysis; Phase 12/13 optional embodiment context; Phase 14 dashboard.
- **Ablation use:** A7 reporting.
- **Dashboard/card use:** regime timeline, trust allocation, stop-loss view, risk explanation, stress-regime view, embodiment-risk view, ablation comparison, RegimeCard, trust-state plots, temporal-failure audits.
- **Paper/thesis claim:** temporal trust proxy, temporal unreliability, static-threshold limitation, regime-aware decision comparison, and interpretability claims only. No clinical fatigue or neurological-state diagnosis.
- **Required source records:** WindowRecord, PredictionRecord, CalibrationRecord when available, UncertaintyRecord, EvidenceQualityRecord where available, IHARQDecisionRecord where available, optional StressProfileRecord, TransitionRecord, EmbodimentState/Outcome records only in declared simulation/proxy mode, SubjectProfileRecord as auxiliary context.
- **Required fields:** source RegimeStateRecord IDs, optional TrustStateRecord IDs, timeline/trust/stop-loss artifact IDs, matched/negative-control IDs, limitations, warning tags, config hashes, export IDs.
- **Optional fields:** stress_profile_id, embodiment_state_id, transition_id, policy_action_id, calibration_drift_score, channel_dropout_score, model_family_shift_score, drift/fatigue/dropout flags, recovery status, evaluation_label, negative-control IDs, dashboard export IDs.
- **Controlled vocabulary fields:** regime labels, risk bands, risk trend, trust target type, trust band, update source, stop-loss status, recommendation, reason codes, claim-boundary tags, DiagnosticOnlyFlags.
- **Lineage envelope class:** temporal derived record or evaluation artifact.
- **Required global lineage fields:** as listed at the start of Section 8; temporal location and source-record IDs are mandatory.
- **Required-if-applicable lineage fields:** `iharq_decision_id`, `evidence_quality_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `transition_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `policy_id`, `dashboard_export_id`, `card_id`, `claim_id`, `ablation_id`, `metric_dictionary_id`, `matched_comparison_key`.
- **Forbidden lineage fields:** non-causal future information in decision-time regime estimation; clinical fatigue labels unless explicitly public and claim-safe; hidden dashboard-edited state.
- **Validation rules:** temporal ordering; causal cutoff; split isolation; finite scores; aligned IDs; simulation/proxy tags; optional trust-state linkage; stop-loss trigger trace; negative-control/matched-comparison completeness for A7 claims.
- **Split/leakage constraints:** rolling windows must not cross forbidden split boundaries or read future labels/outcomes; correctness/outcomes are evaluation-only unless legally past in a declared online/simulation protocol.
- **Simulation/proxy/clinical boundary:** drift, fatigue-like, dropout-risk, and unsafe labels are proxy operating-state labels; stress/embodiment contexts are simulation/proxy-only.
- **Failure modes:** future-information leakage, non-causal features, proxy labels overclaimed as physiological diagnoses, unstable labels, stop-loss untested, trust scores not used or untraceable, missing negative controls, unmatched regime-aware comparison.
- **Missingness interpretation:** missing temporal ordering blocks Layer 5; missing IHARQ history weakens decision-relevance; missing trust-state rows only matters when independent trust timelines are consumed; missing negative controls blocks A7 improvement claim.
- **Canonical name:** `RegimeCard lineage`.
- **Allowed internal aliases:** implementation-local names such as `regime_risk`, `regime_timeline`, `trust_scores`, or `stop_loss_log` only when mapped to canonical exports.
- **Display aliases:** RegimeRisk state, temporal trust state, trust timeline, stop-loss warnings, RegimeRisk card.
- **Deprecated aliases:** none explicitly defined.
- **Forbidden aliases:** clinical fatigue detector, neurological state detector, patient-risk monitor, medical safety controller, or any name that removes proxy/non-clinical limitations.
- **Repository location:** see Section 17; canonical homes include `records/regime_state_records/`, `records/trust_state_records/`, `records/evaluation_outcome_records/layer5_regimerisk/`, with timeline/trust/stop-loss artifacts linked through manifests and cards.
- **Lifecycle stage:** planned/draft_schema until implemented; promoted_to_canonical only after validation.
- **Schema maturity:** draft_schema from architecture; thesis_ready_schema only after implementation validation, negative controls, dashboard lineage, and claim-evidence linkage.
- **Branch status:** target/stretch for RegimeRisk; simulation_only/proxy_only for stress/embodiment-derived fields; optional/future_work for sequence-model regime estimator.
- **Promotion rule:** promote only if causal temporal features, source IDs, configs, thresholds, reason codes, validation status, and claim tags are complete.
- **Diagnostic-only condition:** temporal leakage, missing source IDs, missing A7 matched comparison, missing shuffled/random negative control when claimed, missing metric dictionary, or absent limitation tags.
- **Thesis-ready condition:** valid causal timeline, matched regime-aware/unaware comparison where improvement is claimed, metric dictionary, negative-control report, negative-result note visibility, RegimeCard/dashboard lineage, claim-evidence entry, Layer 0 limitations.
- **Clean source-record status:** derived from clean source records; not allowed to overwrite public-data, prediction, calibration, uncertainty, or IHARQ source records.
- **Allowed derivations:** regime timelines, trust plots, stop-loss summaries, dashboard metrics, RegimeCards, matched-comparison reports, stress/embodiment diagnostic summaries, claim-evidence entries.
- **Forbidden mutations:** rewriting upstream records, post-hoc tuning on test outcomes, using future outcomes, treating stress/embodiment proxy outcomes as clinical observations, dashboard edits to regime state.
- **Source claim-boundary tags:** public_eeg_only, temporal_trust_proxy, proxy_readiness, not_clinical_validation, not_real_patient_safety; add simulation_only/stress_conditioned/embodiment_proxy_only when used.
- **Strictest claim boundary:** temporal trust proxy; no medical fatigue/health-state diagnosis.
- **Example minimal instance:** No concrete minimal instance is included because valid IDs/values would need to be invented.

###### 17.1 Tool-anchor and method-anchor cards
- **IHARQ reliability card:** must link to IHARQ evidence-verification anchors, action-token/display-label mapping, reason-code tables, request/combine traces, fallback/unsafe records, trace completeness, matched-ablation lineage, and claim boundary.
- **RegimeCard:** must link to drift, non-stationarity, rolling reliability, temporal trust, and RegimeRisk anchors, while warning that RegimeRisk is not a medical fatigue or health-state diagnosis.
- **Implementation tool cards:** exact tool versions are not specified in the architecture and must be filled during implementation. Candidate tool/library families include Pandas/Polars, NumPy/SciPy, scikit-learn or equivalent shallow models, YAML config handling, plotting libraries, schema-validation tools, dashboard framework, and optional MNE/pyRiemann/decoder stack anchors where implemented.

###### 3.7 Global dashboard obligations

Layer 10 may read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, export, and package saved records. It must not silently create primary evidence, train/tune models or policies, mutate rewards/stress schedules, repair missing records, or alter claim boundaries. Dashboard-generated views, cards, figures, tables, and export manifests are not primary evidence unless fully traceable to source records, configs, seeds, metric dictionaries, matched-comparison reports, and claim-evidence artifacts.

###### 13.2 Dashboard-generated outputs

Layer 10 may generate dashboard views, cards, figures, tables, export manifests, missingness reports, warning surfaces, ablation summaries, claim-trace views, and reproducibility exports from saved Layer 6–7 records. These outputs must be classified as `dashboard_view_artifact`, `card_artifact`, `figure_table_artifact`, or `manifest_artifact`, not as hidden primary evidence.

Required cards/views for this target scope include:

- Layer 6 adaptive policy overview, evidence-quality card, Adaptive-IHARQ card, learning-to-defer card, contextual-bandit/RL controller cards, policy ablation table, matched-comparison view, reward/cost sensitivity view, negative-result notes, and controller-card export.
- Layer 7 closed-loop session timeline, policy comparison dashboard, matched-comparison dashboard, evidence-request view, stress-conditioned policy view, RegimeRisk-aware view, reward decomposition view, safety-event view, training-vs-frozen-evaluation view, embodiment view where Layer 9 is active, and negative-result view.
- Reproducibility artifacts: dashboard export manifest, figure/table manifest, run/config/seed manifest, controller/environment cards, policy-update trace card when applicable, reward configuration card, safety-event card, and reproducibility card.

Dashboard lineage validation requires source record IDs, metric dictionary entries, configuration hashes, seeds, phase IDs, ablation IDs where applicable, and claim-boundary tags. Any dashboard artifact lacking these must be marked `dashboard_lineage_status: invalid_or_unresolved` and `primary_evidence_status: not_primary_evidence`.

| Stress dashboard | Layer 8 stress profiles/schedules/metrics/manifests/failure taxonomy | stress cards, robustness curves, stress warnings, stress export package | Not primary evidence; derived from Layer 8 records and evaluation artifacts. | Require matched clean/stressed keys and stress limitation tags. |

| Final reproducibility package | All validated records, configs, seeds, metric dictionaries, matched reports, claim-evidence matrix, cards, figures, export manifests | `ReproducibilityManifest`, artifact manifest, export logs, thesis-ready package | Reproducibility evidence only. | A missing manifest lineage downgrades the export package to incomplete/non-thesis-ready. |

###### 3.6 Global ablation IDs relevant to Layers 4-5
- **A0-A4:** upstream baselines that Layer 4 must compare against where applicable.
- **A5:** IHARQ-lite; primary Layer 4 evaluation use.
- **A6:** IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator; Layer 4 participates, but learned estimator ownership belongs to Layer 6 when enabled.

###### IHARQAblationRecord

- **Record category:** evaluation_artifact.
- **Owning layer:** Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification. For `EvidenceQualityRecord`, merge reconciliation must preserve that Layer 4 produces the rule-derived version while Layer 6 may produce a learned version when enabled.
- **Producer module:** Layer 4 ablation and matched-comparison exporter.
- **Consumer layers/modules:** Evaluation scripts, Layer 10, thesis ablation chapter.
- **Created in implementation phase:** Phase 4, except shared or downstream-learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants that may also be created in Phase 6.
- **Validated in implementation phase:** Phase 4 validation gate; dashboard/export validation Phase 14; final thesis evidence Phase 15.
- **Consumed starting in phase:** Phase 5 for IHARQ histories consumed by RegimeRisk; Phase 6 for policy context; Phase 8 for simulation; Phase 12/13 for optional embodiment through simulation-compatible gating; Phase 14 for dashboard.
- **Ablation use:** A5 primary; A6/A7 participation; A0-A4 are baselines/controls, not owners.
- **Dashboard/card use:** IHARQ timeline, evidence-flow view, reason-code distribution, request/combine view, fallback view, unsafe-event view, baseline comparison view, ablation view, matched-comparison view, stress-conditioned IHARQ view, trace-completeness view, IHARQ reliability card, claim-evidence coverage view.
- **Paper/thesis claim:** computational evidence-verification and proxy readiness-control claim only; no clinical safety, patient-safety, real rehabilitation, medical-device, or real muscle stimulation claim.
- **Required source records:** PredictionRecord, CalibrationRecord where calibrated mode is used, UncertaintyRecord, WindowRecord/WindowHistoryRecord where temporal logic is used, ArtifactFlagRecord where signal/channel safety is inspected, ThresholdRegistryRecord, optional RegimeStateRecord, optional model/channel/agreement helper views, and evaluation artifacts only after decision.
- **Required fields:** global/local ablation IDs, ablated variant, source records, decisions and metrics, matched key, metric dictionary, diagnostic flag, negative-result note, claim-evidence pointer.
- **Optional fields:** stress context, embodiment compatibility, simulation outcome/evaluation outcome, trust weights, conformal proxies, negative-result note IDs, dashboard export IDs, local ablation IDs, diagnostic flags, and branch-specific fields when applicable.
- **Controlled vocabulary fields:** IHARQ action tokens, reason-code categories, validation status, evaluation mode, ablation ID, claim-boundary tags, DiagnosticOnlyFlag, fallback routes, unsafe trigger classes.
- **Lineage envelope class:** source-derived decision/evaluation record.
- **Required global lineage fields:** as listed at the start of Section 8; `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `iharq_decision_id` where applicable, `metric_dictionary_id`, `matched_comparison_key` for evaluation rows.
- **Required-if-applicable lineage fields:** `regime_state_id`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `embodiment_run_id`, `transition_id`, `policy_id`, `dashboard_export_id`, `claim_id`.
- **Forbidden lineage fields:** decision-time use of true label, future correctness, future reward, future stress outcome, or hidden dashboard-derived metric.
- **Validation rules:** schema validity; source-record join validity; split/leakage check; action-token validation; reason-code presence; threshold registry legality; matched-comparison completeness for evaluation; dashboard trace completeness for thesis export.
- **Split/leakage constraints:** threshold/calibration/IHARQ rule tuning must not use held-out test outcomes; evaluation labels are post-decision only.
- **Simulation/proxy/clinical boundary:** public EEG and simulated/proxy readiness only. Unsafe/fallback/stop language is computational or simulation-bounded.
- **Failure modes:** missing reason code, missing source record, invalid probability vector, ID mismatch, unregistered threshold, hidden fallback, unsafe overclaim, unmatched comparison, dashboard-only metric, negative result omitted.
- **Missingness interpretation:** missing required fields block thesis-ready output or trigger explicit degraded/diagnostic mode. Optional missingness must be represented, not assumed clean.
- **Canonical name:** `IHARQAblationRecord`.
- **Allowed internal aliases:** implementation-local snake_case filenames or table names only if exported to the canonical name.
- **Display aliases:** human-readable dashboard labels such as IHARQ decision, fallback log, unsafe-event table, evidence quality, IHARQ trace, or IHARQ ablation table.
- **Deprecated aliases:** none explicitly defined in the architecture.
- **Forbidden aliases:** aliases that rewrite Layer 4 stored action tokens, treat no-action as a Layer 4 canonical action token, call unsafe a clinical safety decision, or rename ordinary ensemble voting as IHARQ.
- **Repository location:** see Section 17; canonical homes include `records/iharq_records/`, `records/evidence_quality_records/`, `records/evaluation_outcome_records/layer4_iharq/`, with run-local exports under Layer 4 results where configured.
- **Lifecycle stage:** planned/draft_schema until implemented; promoted_to_canonical only after validation and run provenance.
- **Schema maturity:** draft_schema from architecture; thesis_ready_schema only after implementation validators pass.
- **Branch status:** core/target for A5 IHARQ-lite; stretch/simulation-only/proxy-only when stress or embodiment context is used.
- **Promotion rule:** promote from run-specific record to canonical family only if schema, lineage, config hash, seed, source-record IDs, validation status, and claim tags are complete.
- **Diagnostic-only condition:** unmatched comparison, missing metric dictionary, missing trace, missing source IDs, evaluation leakage, missing negative-result note, or missing dashboard/export lineage.
- **Thesis-ready condition:** valid source records, legal thresholds, complete reason/action trace, matched comparisons where claims compare variants, metric dictionary, negative-result visibility, dashboard/card/export lineage, claim-evidence entry, Layer 0 limitations.
- **Clean source-record status:** not a clean upstream source record; derived_record.
- **Allowed derivations:** dashboard metrics, cards, figures, tables, evaluation summaries, stress-conditioned copies, matched-comparison reports, claim-evidence entries.
- **Forbidden mutations:** rewriting source Prediction/Calibration/Uncertainty/Window records, retuning thresholds post hoc, changing stored action tokens, adding evaluation labels to decision-time records, overwriting clean records with stress/simulation/dashboard edits.
- **Source claim-boundary tags:** public_eeg_only, proxy_readiness, computational_evidence_verification, not_clinical_validation. Add simulation_only, stress_conditioned, embodiment_proxy_only, or diagnostic_only when applicable.
- **Strictest claim boundary:** computational/proxy evidence-verification; never clinical safety.
- **Example minimal instance:** not provided for this registry entry because the architecture gives field requirements but not enough concrete valid row values without inventing IDs, except for Layer 5 RegimeStateRecord where an illustrative example appears in the source architecture.

###### 10.2 Ablation-step vocabulary
Ablation IDs are evaluation-use metadata only. `A5` means IHARQ-lite, `A6` means IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator, and `A7` means IHARQ plus RegimeRisk. `A12` and `A13` may reference stress/embodiment use of Layer 4-5 outputs but do not own those outputs.

## 17. Repository and Storage Registry

### 17.1 Repository/storage merge rule
Repository and storage expectations are grouped by configuration artifacts, canonical records, run-specific records, reports, dashboard exports, cards, figures/tables, manifests, reproducibility packages, and tool/method anchor cards. Explicit paths are preserved. Conceptual paths remain marked as conceptual until final repository confirmation.

###### 17.1 Tool-anchor and method-anchor cards
- **IHARQ reliability card:** must link to IHARQ evidence-verification anchors, action-token/display-label mapping, reason-code tables, request/combine traces, fallback/unsafe records, trace completeness, matched-ablation lineage, and claim boundary.
- **RegimeCard:** must link to drift, non-stationarity, rolling reliability, temporal trust, and RegimeRisk anchors, while warning that RegimeRisk is not a medical fatigue or health-state diagnosis.
- **Implementation tool cards:** exact tool versions are not specified in the architecture and must be filled during implementation. Candidate tool/library families include Pandas/Polars, NumPy/SciPy, scikit-learn or equivalent shallow models, YAML config handling, plotting libraries, schema-validation tools, dashboard framework, and optional MNE/pyRiemann/decoder stack anchors where implemented.

## 18. Failure, Missingness, and Defensive Design Registry

### 18.1 Failure/missingness merge rule
Every missing artifact or validation failure must have a stated effect. Failure categories include missingness, validation failure, schema failure, lineage failure, split/leakage failure, claim-safety failure, dashboard failure, consumer failure, fallback behavior, negative-result interpretation, repair action, and diagnostic-only downgrade.

### 18.2 Source-preserved failure, missingness, and defensive-design rules

### 18.S Source-preserved detail — Layers 0–1
###### 3.1.12 Failure, missingness, and defensive-design repair patch

| Entity / class | Failure or missingness | Cross-layer consequence | Repair / fallback | Diagnostic-only downgrade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DatasetRecord` missing or invalid | dataset identity/source/access boundary unresolved | Blocks Layer 2 and all downstream evidence rooted in the dataset | repair dataset card/source metadata or exclude dataset with logged reason | yes |
| `WindowRecord` missing or invalid | no stable unit of prediction/calibration/replay | Blocks decoder, calibration, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, policy, simulation, stress, and dashboard lineage | regenerate versioned windows under Phase 1 protocol; preserve repair log | yes |
| `SplitRecord` failed/leaky | train/test/calibration leakage risk | Blocks metric claims, calibration claims, policy claims, stress comparisons, and embodiment comparisons | rebuild split protocol and revalidate; mark prior runs diagnostic-only | yes |
| `LabelMapRecord` ambiguous | label semantics or class order unclear | invalidates metrics, calibration, action correctness, pseudo-label construction | repair label map with versioned update and rerun dependent outputs | yes |
| `PreprocessingRecord` missing | transformations not reproducible | comparisons unmatched; calibration/IHARQ lineage incomplete | create or restore preprocessing manifest; rerun affected outputs | yes |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` missing where needed | hidden missingness/exclusion risk | downstream failure/quality claims incomplete | create artifact/exclusion report; propagate warnings | yes |
| `ValidationReport` failed | schema, split, label, leakage, or missingness issue | downstream phase gate remains closed | repair source records or explicitly mark excluded/diagnostic | yes |
| `Layer1Manifest` incomplete | source bundle unreproducible | dashboard export and final evidence package incomplete | rebuild manifest from saved records/hashes/configs | yes |
| `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` incomplete | matched comparison keys not complete | A0–A13 comparisons become unmatched or diagnostic-only | repair matching keys; produce negative-result/diagnostic flags | yes |
| Layer 0 claim artifact missing | final claim lacks governance trace | paper/dashboard claim not thesis-ready | create claim ledger/evidence matrix or downgrade/remove claim | yes |
| Dashboard warning suppressed | limitation/missingness hidden | invalid dashboard or paper evidence | restore warning surface and export manifest | yes |
| Clean source record overwritten | source-record immutability violation | all affected downstream derived results not thesis-ready | recreate as versioned record, preserve old record, emit repair/supersession log | yes |

###### 18. Failure, Missingness, and Defensive Design

| Entity | Missingness / failure | Effect | Fallback behavior | Negative-result interpretation | Repair action | Diagnostic-only downgrade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DatasetRecord | Missing source, unresolved license/source version, incomplete metadata | Dataset unusable for source-grounded evaluation | Exclude dataset or mark optional/future | Dataset limitation recorded | Regenerate with source metadata; do not fake fields | yes |
| WindowRecord | Missing windows, wrong timing, label missing, overlap leakage | Decoder and downstream records blocked | Regenerate windows from valid protocol | Failed protocol readiness | Regenerate versioned record bundle | yes |
| SplitRecord | Leakage failure, missing seed, missing calibration/adaptation membership | Matched comparison invalid | Block evaluation or regenerate split | Comparison not confirmatory | Create new split version and validation report | yes |
| PreprocessingRecord | Missing config hash, illegal normalization fit scope | Decoder/calibration invalid | Block or rerun preprocessing with legal config | Preprocessing limitation | New preprocessing version | yes |
| LabelMapRecord | Unmapped or ambiguous label | Affected task/dataset invalid | Exclude label/task or mark diagnostic | Label ambiguity disclosed | Update labels.yaml and regenerate versioned map | yes |
| ArtifactFlagRecord | Missing flags or invalid severity/action | Quality warnings incomplete | Treat absent flags as unknown, not clean | Missingness warning | Regenerate or mark unavailable | optional/diagnostic depending on use |
| ValidationReport | Missing/failing validation | Downstream evidence not thesis-ready | Block promotion/export | Validation failure note | Run auditor and preserve failure report | yes |
| DatasetCard / ProtocolCard | Missing source lineage | Card not thesis-ready | Do not display as final evidence | Documentation gap | Regenerate from records | yes |
| Layer1Manifest | Broken path, stale hash, missing record | Reproducibility incomplete | Block final package | Reproduction gap | Regenerate manifest after records validate | yes |
| Ablation readiness artifact | Missing matched keys or validation status | A0–A13 comparisons blocked/diagnostic | Show readiness warning | Evaluation gap | Regenerate from manifest and validation report | yes |
| ClaimLedger / ClaimEvidenceMatrix | Missing claim-to-artifact trace | Final claims cannot be approved | Block or downgrade claim | Claim gap disclosed | Create/repair trace with source records and limitations | yes |
| Layer 0 limitation tags | Missing inherited limitations | Overclaim risk | Apply strictest default limitation and block stronger claim | Claim-safety failure | Restore limitation inheritance | yes/block |

Every missing artifact has an explicit effect; no missing Layer 1 source or Layer 0 claim artifact may be silently ignored.
