# R24 Layer 2 Post-Finalization Registry Synchronization Addendum

## R24.1 Purpose and scope

This addendum applies the stable semantic, content, producer-consumer, validation, lifecycle, and visibility profiles established by the finalized Layer 2 M7 Nuts-and-Bolts specification. It resolves the Registry side of the 38 `REG-L2-MS-*` controlled-intake cards wherever M7 provides a stable architecture-safe answer. It does not canonicalize implementation paths, numerical experiment settings, fitted values, live record instances, or new object families.

## R24.2 Layer 2 canonical and governed output profiles

### `PredictionRecord` — `canonical_record`

**Sole canonical writer:** Prediction logger.  
**Required governance:** `record_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `producer_layer`, `validation_status`, `created_timestamp`, `config_hash`, immutable source IDs and source versions.  
**Required lineage:** dataset, subject, optional session/run, trial/source-event and window identity, split and split role, label budget, preprocessing and label-map identities, model/decoder/family identity, seed and repetition identity.  
**Required prediction contract:** `predicted_class`, typed native output or declared hard-label-only state, `score_type`, exact `class_order`, output cardinality/layout, missing-score reason when applicable, temporal/order fields when required.  
**Evaluation-only overlay:** `label_true`, correctness and truth-derived error labels are access-controlled evaluation fields and are forbidden from decision/A4/downstream feature views.  
**Validation:** class-set equality, ordered-axis consistency, finite score checks, score/cardinality compatibility, split legality, source-reference closure, temporal monotonicity where required, no forbidden future/policy/embodiment fields.  
**Lifecycle:** immutable after validation; correction creates a successor and invalidates dependent derived artifacts.

### `ModelRegistryRecord` — `canonical_record`

**Writer:** Model-family registry.  
**Content:** model/decoder/family/name; accepted method role; implementation identity and source revision; Layer 1 input-manifest/config identities; model-local transform identity and fit scope; training/validation/tuning policy; complete hyperparameters; label budget; seed/repetition; resource evidence; checkpoint/artifact identities and hashes; native score type and class order; training terminal and failure reason; environment/dependency/licence/provenance; reload-equivalence result.  
**Prediction linkage:** C1 writes immutable version 1 before predictions exist. C2 predictions forward-reference exact model ID/version/hash. If a reverse prediction collection link is required, the Model-family registry writes an immutable successor version; C2 never mutates the record.  
**Lifecycle:** validated versions are never overwritten; supersession and dependency invalidation are explicit.

### `BaselineMetricRecord` — `metric_artifact / canonical metric record`

Required content includes metric dictionary identity/version, source prediction collection and matched-comparison key, dataset/model/budget/split/seed identities, participant/session aggregation scope, complete denominator and missing/unresolved counts, value and direction, interval/seed summary where applicable, diagnostic-only and unmatched flags, and source hashes. Exact metric formula and statistical settings remain Protocol v1.0-owned.

### `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` — `metric_artifact / canonical record`

Required content includes ordered legal budgets, nested-subset identities, source predictions and baseline metrics, metric dictionary links, participant/session aggregation, seed/repetition summaries, support counts, invalid/sparse budget reasons, intervals where approved, curve/version identity and inherited limitation flags.

### `SubjectProfileRecord` — `derived_record / canonical profile record`

Required content is descriptive only: participant/session identity, eligible/successful/common-support model IDs, coverage/opportunity-set counts, descriptor validity map, omitted-descriptor reasons, split/budget/source IDs, common-support performance/rank/stability/oracle-gap descriptors where valid, and diagnostic all-available descriptors when separately labeled. Categorical easy/difficult diagnosis, physiological inference and policy-routing authority are forbidden.

### `EnsembleControlRecord` — `derived_record / evaluation_artifact`

Required content includes control type, fixed member IDs/versions/hashes, window/aggregation identity, compatible score/class contract, missing-member policy, zero-member terminal state, hard-vote counts, authorized probability tie-break over tied classes, compatible equal-weight native-probability average where selected, unresolved counts, member disagreement, delay/burden, complete denominators, matched keys, and A4 identity. Registered threshold selection, calibration, rejection and selective prediction are forbidden.

### `FailureCaseIndex` — `warning_or_failure_log / evaluation_artifact`

Two-level logical content is applied: (1) an immutable index header with source snapshot, scope, filters, generation config and counts; and (2) entries linking source prediction/run/model/budget/participant/session IDs, failure class, diagnostic-only state, high-confidence-wrong candidate fields where legal, failed/skipped/unsupported evidence, and limitation notes. It is evaluation-only and never a decision-time feature source.

### `Layer2ReadinessReport` — `validation_report`

**Sole final writer:** Downstream readiness validator.  
Required content is branch×consumer specific and includes source snapshot identity, required and available record/artifact/schema/score/class/time/budget/profile/control fields, missing prerequisites, warnings, diagnostic/block reasons, stale/superseded dependencies, compatibility result and source hashes. Readiness cannot improve when failures, missingness or staleness increase. It is a compatibility gate, not a scientific-success or safety decision.

### Other governed Layer 2 evidence

- `LeakageWarningRecord`: source split IDs, affected records/branches, leakage condition, severity, required action and final-evaluation block/diagnostic scope.
- `MatchedComparisonReport`: exact matched keys, eligible rows, exclusions, denominator reconciliation, metric identities and confirmatory/diagnostic status.
- `NegativeResultNote`: scientifically meaningful failure/insufficiency, affected source IDs, interpretation boundary and disclosure requirement.
- `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`: affected object/version, reason, source evidence, propagation scope and removal only through controlled successor validation.
- trained model/checkpoint artifacts, attempt/training/validation/inference/reload/resource/failure logs, card-source bundles, Layer 10 snapshot/export sources and Phase 2 handoff packages remain governed supporting artifacts, not newly invented canonical record families.

## R24.3 Independent status-axis rule

The following axes must remain separate and machine-readable:

1. Method-selection role/disposition;
2. planned/run terminal state;
3. schema/semantic validation status;
4. artifact lifecycle state;
5. branch×consumer readiness;
6. claim/diagnostic limitation scope.

Compound pseudo-status strings that concatenate these axes are forbidden. Exact values use the effective Registry vocabularies and reason fields.

# R25 Layer 2 Bidirectional Registry Synchronization Addendum

## R25.1 Authority boundary

R24's applied profiles remain unchanged. R25 binds them to compatibility set `L2-NB-M8-BIDIRECTIONAL-SYNC-R2-20260718` and adds reverse propagation. The Registry remains authoritative for canonical/governed names, object classes, field envelopes, vocabularies, producer-consumer contracts, validation, lifecycle, visibility and open-issue disposition. M8 may supply technical evidence and propose a Registry change, but it may not create or mutate canonical schema locally.

## R25.2 Record-to-design two-way map

| Registry object/profile | Registry authority retained | M8 realization | Reverse trigger into M8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PredictionRecord` | canonical identity, sole writer, fields, validation, immutability | C2 constructs class/score/time/reference-safe records | any field/writer/lifecycle change updates C2 transformation and all downstream consumers |
| `ModelRegistryRecord` | canonical model identity, provenance, lifecycle and links | C1 writes immutable versions and governed late links | link/field/lifecycle change updates C1 registry, C2 references, C3 closure and reload tests |
| `BaselineMetricRecord` | metric artifact identity and source linkage | C2 produces participant-first A0/A4 metric sources | metric field/producer change updates Protocol mapping and C2/C3 validation |
| `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` | canonical curve identity and lineage | C2 builds legal nested-budget curves | budget/support/field change updates curve algorithm and consumer readiness |
| `SubjectProfileRecord` | `derived_record / canonical profile record`; descriptive boundary | C2 computes common-support descriptors | class/visibility change updates profiling, Layer 5/6/10 eligibility and claim limits |
| `EnsembleControlRecord` | `derived_record / evaluation_artifact`; ordinary A4 boundary | C2 writes fixed-member vote/average/control evidence | A4 field or lifecycle change updates aggregation and Protocol matching |
| `FailureCaseIndex` | warning/failure evaluation artifact and visibility | C3 indexes immutable source failures | privacy/entry/header/lifecycle change updates C3 index and Layer 10 views |
| `Layer2ReadinessReport` | validation report identity and C3 sole final writer | C3 computes branch×consumer readiness | prerequisite/status/lifecycle change updates monotonicity and all consumer gates |
| `LeakageWarningRecord` | governed warning identity and blocking scope | originator writes; C3 propagates | severity/field change updates split guards, release and Layer 0 visibility |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | governed evaluation artifact identity | C2 writes; C3 validates | matched-key/status change updates A0/A4 and thesis-facing eligibility |
| `NegativeResultNote` | governed negative-evidence identity | originating function writes; C3 packages | trigger/visibility change updates denominator, card and claim evidence |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | governed claim-scope indicator | originator writes; C3 propagates | reason/removal/lifecycle change updates readiness and every downstream consumer |

## R25.3 Reverse Registry workflow

```text
M8/implementation evidence indicates schema or lifecycle insufficiency
→ create Registry Impact candidate with affected records, fields, producers, consumers and migration impact
→ Registry owner accepts/modifies/rejects/defers
→ issue Registry successor
→ issue Layer 2 successor
→ migrate or supersede affected artifacts; rerun validators and readiness
```

A local helper payload stays noncanonical unless this workflow approves it. Physical paths, classes, serializer formats and database technology remain Build Book-owned.

## R25.4 Controlled-intake and issue continuity

The 38 `REG-L2-MS-*` dispositions in R24 remain effective. The nine `L2-OI-*` issues retain their R24 owner outcomes: Registry-side closures remain closed; Protocol-owned metric/run matters remain Protocol-owned; Build-owned physical serialization remains Build-owned. A closed issue reopens only when new evidence invalidates the applied profile, not merely because implementation has begun.

## R25.5 Compatibility and no-drift

The effective technical realization is M8. Any use of R25 with M7/M6 or a different Plan/Protocol/Playbook set requires an impact review. Historical wording inside preserved predecessors remains audit history only.

# R26 Layer 4 Post-Method-Selection Controlled-Intake Addendum

**Applied status:** `CURRENT-STAGE SYNCHRONIZATION APPLIED`  
**Compatibility set:** `L4-METHOD-SELECTION-POST-FINALIZATION-SYNC-R1-20260718`  
**Prepared:** 18 July 2026

## 1. Authority and application rule

This applied addendum is the controlling owner-review overlay for Layer 4 post-method-selection intake. It is installed as a versioned controlled-intake section governed through the Registry's existing impact/patch ledger. Card-level candidate wording remains noncanonical until the Registry owner records an accepted disposition and effective version.

Precedence remains Architecture → Registry → Plan → Protocol → Playbook → upstream registers/N&B → Layer 4 Register. The Layer 4 Register supplies selected semantics; it does not self-authorize canonical fields.

## 2. Required disposition classes

Every card receives exactly one final disposition:

```text
NO-PATCH / EXISTING CONTRACT SUFFICIENT
PROFILE-ONLY / EXISTING OBJECT
CONSOLIDATE EXISTING OPEN ISSUE
ALIAS OR VOCABULARY CLARIFICATION
VALIDATION OR CARDINALITY CLARIFICATION
LIFECYCLE / PRODUCER-CONSUMER CLARIFICATION
SCHEMA PATCH APPROVED
DEFERRED / BLOCKED PENDING EVIDENCE
REJECTED AS DUPLICATE OR OUT OF SCOPE
```

A schema patch is approved only after proving that an existing record, generic lineage/status field, content profile, validation profile, alias map, supporting artifact or manifest cannot represent the accepted method.

## 4. Canonical invariants that cannot change

- exactly thirteen Layer 4 modules/support submodules;
- exactly seven stored actions: `accept, wait, request_evidence, combine_evidence, fallback, uncertain, unsafe`;
- exactly eight reason parents: `Acceptance, Waiting, Request evidence, Combine evidence, Fallback, Uncertain, Unsafe, System integrity`;
- A0–A13 only; no A14;
- eleven exact local A5 labels;
- Layer 4 rule-derived and Layer 6 learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants remain producer/derivation-distinct;
- helper views remain local/precomputed/inferred candidates unless owner-approved promotion passes the burden of proof;
- consumer actions or commands never rewrite the source Layer 4 action token;
- predecessors remain immutable; corrections create successors and invalidate the dependent closure.

## 5. Product-family content and emission profile

| Product family | Producer | Emission condition | Minimum content purpose | Consumers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IHARQDecisionRecord | Layer 4 / IHARQ rule engine | always: one per decision event | one canonical action; primary/supporting reasons; source/config/budget/threshold/branch/reevaluation links | Layers 5–10; evaluation; audit |
| IHARQTraceRecord | Layer 4 / decision logger | always with every decision | ordered predicate/evidence/budget/action/reason/config lineage; replay digest | Layer 10; debugging; reproducibility; evaluation |
| EvidenceQualityRecord | Layer 4 rule-derived variant; Layer 6 learned variant separately | when rule-derived component evidence is materialized | component states, availability, applicability, support scope, dependence, causal cutoff; no hidden correctness scalar | Layers 4–7; Layer 10; evaluation |
| CombinedEvidenceRecord | Layer 4 / evidence combiner | only when combine_evidence behavior is active and eligibility passes | contributors, relation, dependence, conflict, method/profile, before/after state, burden and result link | Layers 4,6,7,10; evaluation |
| FallbackDecisionRecord | Layer 4 / fallback router | only for fallback selection or failure | registered route, availability/eligibility, reason, burden/cost, success/failure during evaluation, claim boundary | Layers 6,7,9,10; evaluation |
| UnsafeEventRecord | Layer 4 / unsafe-state monitor | only for approved severe computational/proxy trigger | trigger, severity, blocked action, source, recovery/reset, proxy/simulation limitation | Layers 7,9,10; Layer 0 |
| IHARQAblationRecord | Layer 4 / ablation exporter | for A5 and approved eligible local variants | A5 parent, exact local label, branch eligibility, parent config/delta, matched key, diagnostic state | Protocol; Layer 10; thesis |
| Layer 4 EvaluationOutcomeRecord | Layer 4 evaluation exporter | retrospective/evaluation namespace only | decision/trace linkage, metric IDs, denominators, coverage/delay/burden/fallback/unsafe outcomes, limitations | Protocol; Layer 10; Layer 0 |
| MatchedComparisonReport | evaluation exporter / Layer 10 export | for matched A0–A5/local comparisons | complete matched key, comparator eligibility, denominators/attrition, metric versions, missing cells, intervals, negative-result links | Layer 10; Layer 0; thesis |
| MetricDictionaryEntry references/candidates | metric governance / evaluation | whenever a metric is emitted or proposed | definition, direction, unit, denominator, independent unit, aggregation, context, limitations and diagnostic rules | Protocol; Layer 10; Layer 0 |
| NegativeResultNote | evaluation / Layer 10 / failure-governance producer as applicable | for null, adverse, invalid, insufficient-baseline, route-failure or overconservative outcomes | bounded interpretation, affected claim, fallback/diagnostic status, source evidence | Layer 10; Layer 0; thesis |
| DiagnosticOnlyFlag | producer/evaluator at point of downgrade | when evidence/comparison cannot support ordinary claims | reason, scope, affected records/comparisons, consumer restrictions and reopen condition | all downstream consumers |
| Phase 4 manifests and handoff bundles | Layer 4 / decision logger and exporters | input freeze, outputs, gate evidence and consumer handoff | source closure, schema/status/config/rule/taxonomy/metric hashes, conditional outputs, gates, limitations, supersession/invalidation | Layers 5–10; Layer 0; implementation/evaluation |

### 5.1 Cardinality and absence semantics

- one `IHARQDecisionRecord` and one linked `IHARQTraceRecord` per decision event;
- `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord` and `UnsafeEventRecord` are conditional and must not be emitted as empty placeholders;
- absence of a conditional record means the corresponding behavior was not materialized for that event, not that an expected mandatory record is missing;
- a behavior-specific claim requires the conditional record and its decision/trace link;
- reevaluation produces a linked new event/version rather than mutating the predecessor.

## 6. Visibility, missingness and status profile

The owner disposition must preserve separate axes for:

- decision-time, evaluation-only, oracle/headroom and diagnostic visibility;
- required, conditional, unsupported and unavailable evidence;
- valid, invalid, stale, superseded, blocked, failed, diagnostic-only and requires-confirmation states;
- threshold formal compatibility versus support-scope warning;
- causal cutoff and future/outcome prohibition;
- branch-by-consumer readiness.

Unknown or unavailable is never silently treated as clean, favorable, adverse or unsafe.

## 7. Vocabulary and alias profile

- stored actions remain exact; `combine` is at most a mapped display/adapter alias for `combine_evidence`;
- reason parents remain exact; child codes require owner-approved versioned taxonomy and parent mapping;
- local A5 labels remain exact;
- request types, budget states, fallback routes, unsafe triggers, evidence component states and outcome classes require versioned profile/enum disposition before implementation use;
- downstream action/command maps carry source token, mapping ID/version and unsupported-map state.

## 8. Lifecycle, correction and dependency profile

Every accepted profile must define:

- source and predecessor/successor references;
- immutable record identity and semantic profile version;
- stale/superseded/blocked/regenerated status;
- complete dependent-closure invalidation after accepted upstream correction;
- gate/comparison/claim impacts;
- manifest and consumer-readiness update;
- no in-place source repair.

## 9. Producer-consumer and future-layer profile

The owner workbook must validate consumers for Layers 5–10 and Layer 0, including causal Layer 4→5 history, versioned A7 reruns, Layer 6 learned-variant separation, Layer 7 simulation action mapping, Layer 8 clean/stressed separation, Layer 9 source-action preservation, Layer 10 read-only rendering and Layer 0 claim audit.

## 10. Owner workbook fields

For every card record:

```text
card ID
existing object/open issue reused
final disposition and rationale
accepted canonical name/profile/version
producer and all consumers
visibility and causal role
requiredness/cardinality/missingness
validation and status vocabulary
lifecycle/supersession/invalidation
aliases/deprecations
migration/backward compatibility
positive/negative/round-trip fixtures
use-before-approval lint result
owner/reviewer approvals
effective version
affected documents and downstream blockers
```

## 11. Migration and compatibility

- additive profile fields are optional for predecessor readers unless a major schema version is approved;
- required semantic changes demand an explicit profile/schema version and reader rejection behavior;
- aliases/deprecations require bidirectional fixtures where lawful;
- existing IDs remain stable; corrections create successors;
- no candidate field may enter N&B, code or output fixtures before approval;
- rejected/deferred cards keep the corresponding method surface blocked or `requires_confirmation`.

## 12. Acceptance checklist

- [ ] 36 cards disposed with no duplicate issue or parallel schema.
- [ ] all seven actions and eight reason parents preserved.
- [ ] all 13 product families have producer, emission, content, visibility, lifecycle and consumer profiles.
- [ ] conditional cardinality and linked-event fixtures pass.
- [ ] visibility/oracle and future-field rejection fixtures pass.
- [ ] helper views remain local/candidate unless promotion is approved.
- [ ] branch-by-consumer and transitive-invalidation fixtures pass.
- [ ] matched-key/denominator/attrition and negative/diagnostic fixtures pass.
- [ ] Layer 10/0 and downstream consumer tests pass.

## 4. Existing-object and no-substitute lock

The following existing families are reused and remain canonical: `RegimeStateRecord`; conditional `TrustStateRecord`; Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`; `MatchedComparisonReport`; `MetricDictionaryEntry`; `NegativeResultNote`; `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`; `ReproducibilityManifest`; `regime_timelines.csv`; `trust_scores.csv`; `stop_loss_warnings.csv`; `RegimeCard` source-lineage bundle; and the existing Layer 4↔5 and Layer 5→6/7/9/10/0 interface families. Any alternative spelling is only an alias candidate until reversibly mapped and owner-approved.

## 5. Applied intake, visibility and validation profile

- Layer 5 consumption is closed-world by consumer: every record and field is `required`, `conditional`, `evaluation-only`, or unavailable.
- Unknown record/field input is unavailable until a governed monotonic extension is accepted.
- Visibility is one of `decision-time visible`, `delayed-update visible`, `evaluation-only`, or `forbidden`.
- `PRIMARY-FROZEN-A7`, `DELAYED-UPDATE-RESEARCH`, and `ORACLE-HEADROOM` are separate projections/runs.
- Validation is orthogonal and issue-vector based: structural, semantic, causal, split, support/capability, numerical, provenance and claim readiness.
- Failure is quarantined at the narrowest dependency closure; unrelated valid branches may continue.
- Current correctness, future outcomes, descendants and private/debug fields cannot enter the primary runtime projection.

## 6. Applied temporal, causal and horizon profile

- Every temporal input carries or resolves event time, availability time, source identity, authoritative order or partial-order evidence and decision cutoff.
- Eligibility requires strict predecessor status, availability by cutoff, non-descendant status, legal split/reset/configuration identity and inclusion inside the source/key reliable prefix.
- Ambiguous equal-time ordering is ineligible unless authoritative order evidence exists.
- Completeness is source/key scoped and may represent expected-source set, reliable prefix/watermark, idle/stalled/unknown state and lag; one global minimum frontier is prohibited as the sole legality rule.
- Observational chronology identity is separate from monitored target/model/configuration epoch. Compatible bridge versus hard reset and reset reason are preserved.
- Every active horizon is defined by event-count bound, elapsed-time bound, minimum effective observed support and session/context role.

## 7. Applied feature, missingness and helper-view profile

Each typed feature block preserves source record/field, visibility zone, horizon, units, direction, normalization source, effective support, missingness mask, age/staleness, dependency group, validity, estimator status and configuration reference.

Observed evidence plus mask/age/support is primary. Bounded LOCF/causal decay is the transparent comparator. A one-sided uncertainty-aware state-space estimate is conditionally admissible only as a helper view. Estimates never overwrite canonical observations; future/bidirectional primary estimation is forbidden.

## 8. Applied derivation, configuration and lineage profile

- Canonical roots remain immutable.
- Derived views/artifacts are append-only, content-addressed and linked through exact source/config closure.
- Supersession, invalidation reason, protected roots, rebuild status and reconstruction-preserving compaction are mandatory lifecycle semantics.
- Configuration identity distinguishes semantic scientific identity, component identity, derivation identity, operational/environment identity and root-manifest identity.
- Display/path-only changes cannot silently become scientific identity changes; scientific-breaking changes invalidate matching and dependent artifacts.

## 9. `RegimeStateRecord` applied logical content profile

| Field family | Applied content |
|---|---|
| Identity and lineage | record/schema/version identity; run/config/root-manifest identity; frozen seed; dataset/subject/session/trial/window; ordered sequence/replay index; split role; model/model-family; source-record closure; source-lineage reference; causal cutoff; availability/completeness lineage; validation; diagnostic and claim tags |
| Required regime state | regime_label; regime_probability or declared probability-quality status; regime_risk_score; risk_trend; risk_band |
| Risk components | volatility_score; drawdown_score; drift_risk_score; fatigue_like_risk_score; dropout_risk_score; failure_risk_score, each with availability/support/config/contribution provenance |
| Trust and routing | trust summary; trusted_set; conditional TrustStateRecord references; stop_loss_status; recommendation; reason_codes or governed structured explanation |
| Transition and recovery | previous/current state; transition cause; dwell/persistence; hysteresis/reset/bridge status; warning/active/cooldown/recovery/re-entry state |
| Optional context | stress, simulation, transition, policy and embodiment references only when supplied and correctly tagged; otherwise explicit unavailable/null plus source-status |
| Evaluation-only | evaluation label/outcome/control IDs/matched key/metric references only in evaluation projection; forbidden in ordinary runtime projection |

**Cardinality:** one record per eligible target sequence position/configuration/variant projection. Missing or invalid rows are not silently synthesized.  
**Runtime leakage lock:** runtime projection contains no current/future correctness or outcome label.  
**State authority:** transparent hysteretic FSM is the production authority; HSMM and other declared variants use the same canonical state vocabulary and variant/config provenance.

## 10. Conditional `TrustStateRecord` applied profile

`TrustStateRecord` is emitted when trust has an independent lifecycle, registered target identity, downstream consumer, display or claim. When inactive, trust remains a summary/trusted-set field on `RegimeStateRecord` and absence is explicit.

| Field family | Applied content |
|---|---|
| Identity and source linkage | record/schema/version; source RegimeStateRecord ID; dataset/subject/session/trial/window/sequence/time identity; config and split provenance |
| Target and score | trust_target_type; trust_target_id; trust_score; trust_trend; trust_band; trusted_set_membership |
| Update lifecycle | update_source; support and source evidence; decay/recovery; exclusion/re-entry; reason codes/structured explanation |
| Validation and boundaries | validation state; diagnostic-only state; simulation/proxy and claim-boundary tags |

## 11. Evaluation, report and export profiles

- Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` records evaluation mode, primary/diagnostic estimand, event horizon/censoring, outcome visibility, component/config IDs, matched support/attrition, metrics and negative-result disposition.
- `MatchedComparisonReport` requires exact common support and matching identities; unmatched rows are descriptive/diagnostic only.
- Negative-control reports record transformation, seed/block/shift/burden-match parameters, invariants and failure state.
- `regime_timelines.csv`, conditional `trust_scores.csv` and `stop_loss_warnings.csv` carry source record IDs, config/version, validation, diagnostic and claim tags; no hidden Layer 10 recomputation is permitted.
- Every warning/trust row links to its source state and target; orphan rows are invalid.

## 12. Component and model provenance profile

The existing `RegimeStateRecord` component fields/refs preserve method/config identity and support for robust MAD/IQR/EWMA volatility, causal drawdown/reference/recovery, uncertainty-distribution drift plus ADWIN/PH/KSWIN and conditional confirmation evidence, dropout/source availability, fatigue-like diagnostic gating, runtime failure proxy and evaluation-only complete/censored target branch, grouped monotone RegimeRisk, FSM state authority and conditional HSMM adjunct.

No component creates a new canonical record family. Detailed statistics, detector events and model internals remain helper/config/evaluation artifacts unless separately approved for cross-consumer serialization.

## 13. Exact vocabulary and explanation policy

```text
regime_label: stable | noisy | drift-risk | fatigue-risk | dropout-risk | uncertain | unsafe
risk_band: low | moderate | high | critical
risk_trend: rising | falling | stable | recovering (or a Registry-permitted numeric slope)
stop_loss_status: none | warning | active | fallback recommended | no-action recommended | unsafe recommended
recommendation: normal | stricter evidence | trusted-set restriction | fallback | no-action | unsafe | cooldown | recovery monitoring
trust_target_type: decoder | model family | evidence source | channel subset | window group | fallback route
trust_band: low | moderate | high | unusable
update_source: label-based | label-free proxy | stress-derived | simulation-derived | evaluation-only
IHARQ action history: accept | wait | request_evidence | combine_evidence | fallback | uncertain | unsafe
```

No new Layer 5 reason token is introduced here. Canonical tokens already present in the Registry may be emitted. Structured component/source explanations—including contributions, transition/threshold trigger, source IDs, validity/support and config—are authorized as governed supporting content. A missing canonical token emits no fabricated token and opens the existing Registry patch path.

## 14. Interface and ownership profile

- Layer 4→5: immutable A5 `IHARQDecisionRecord`/`IHARQTraceRecord` histories, canonical tokens, strict predecessor and no same-step cycle.
- Layer 5→4 A7 feedback: separately versioned rerun, exact source-state/config/matched-key linkage, original A5 unchanged.
- Layer 5→6: reference-only regime/trust/stop-loss context; Layer 6 retains policy/action ownership.
- Layer 5→7/8/9: frozen/update, clean/stressed and lagged embodiment context are explicitly tagged; Layer 5 does not own transitions, stress or embodiment.
- Layer 5→10: read-only source bundle; Layer 10 may render but not recompute/retune/mutate.
- Layer 5→0: claim-review pointers and inherited proxy/simulation/nonclinical limitations; Layer 0 retains claim authority.

## 15. Phase 5 manifest and staged-freeze profile

Phase 5 manifests enumerate every applicable official output, source closure, source and artifact hashes, decision/config IDs, gate status, consumer acceptance, evidence cutoff, Registry disposition, blockers and controlled-reopen predicates. Method-selection, Registry, Nuts-and-Bolts, Build Book, Protocol, empirical, dashboard and claim readiness are separate facets and may not be collapsed into one atomic `complete` flag.

## 16. Controlled open items

1. A minimum canonical Layer 5 reason-token extension remains owner-gated; structured explanation fallback is active.
2. Exact physical field names/serialization remain to Layer 5 Nuts-and-Bolts and Build Book unless already specified by the preserved Registry.
3. The exact canonical name of the Layer 2/3→5 temporal diagnostic interface remains source-controlled where the predecessor marks it inferred/conditional.
4. Numerical thresholds, horizon values, model hyperparameters and statistical constants remain Protocol v1.0/Nuts-and-Bolts work.

## 17. Migration, reverse propagation and future-layer rule

No existing object is renamed or rewritten. Accepted predecessor corrections create immutable successors and invalidate dependent Layer 5 artifacts by source/config closure. Future Layers 6–10 must cite this R27 successor and M7, consume references rather than local copies, and submit owner-scoped impact cards for any additional field/vocabulary/interface need.

## 18. R27 acceptance checklist

- [x] All 30 owner-review cards have an applied disposition.
- [x] All 15 packages have a final status.
- [x] Existing canonical families are reused.
- [x] Visibility, causality, support, missingness, configuration and lineage profiles are explicit.
- [x] Regime/trust/evaluation/export/interface profiles are explicit.
- [x] A5 remains immutable and A7 separately versioned.
- [x] No A14 or new global ablation is introduced.
- [x] No new reason token is fabricated.
- [x] Open physical-schema/numerical items remain correctly deferred.

## 3. Status-axis normalization

| Axis | Meaning in R28 | What `APPLIED` does not mean |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical family | Existing Registry family remains the object authority | It does not create a new record family |
| Logical content profile | Required/conditional field families and validation semantics are accepted | It does not freeze every serialized field spelling |
| Physical schema | Existing schemas remain valid; additions require N&B/Build evidence and owner acceptance | Method selection alone cannot patch JSON/CSV schemas |
| Vocabulary | Existing canonical tokens and aliases remain controlling | Structured explanation text is not a new token |
| Interface | Existing producer/consumer direction and ownership are clarified | No local code-facing interface name becomes canonical automatically |
| Lifecycle | Immutability, successor, invalidation and rebuild behavior applies | No in-place repair or silent overwrite is permitted |
| Readiness | Method-selection profile is available for downstream design | Runtime evidence and empirical claim readiness remain unproven |

## 7. Core record logical minimums

### 7.1 `RegimeStateRecord`

The existing canonical family must be capable of representing, directly or through accepted references:

- record/schema/run/configuration/seed identity;
- dataset/subject/session/trial/window/sequence/split/model identity;
- source closure, causal cutoff, availability and validation state;
- regime label/probability, RegimeRisk score/band/trend;
- volatility, drawdown, drift, fatigue-like, dropout and failure-risk components with availability/provenance;
- state-transition, persistence, hysteresis and reset evidence;
- trust summary/trusted set references when applicable;
- stop-loss status, recommendation and reason evidence;
- diagnostic-only and claim-boundary tags.

No evaluation label, current correctness or future outcome may enter the ordinary decision-time projection.

### 7.2 Conditional `TrustStateRecord`

An independent trust record is required only when trust has an independent lifecycle, downstream use or claim. It must resolve to its source `RegimeStateRecord` and preserve target type/ID, score/trend/band, trusted-set membership, update source, decay/recovery state, support, reason evidence, configuration, validation and claim tags.

### 7.3 Evaluation/report objects

`EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, negative-control reports, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, Metric Dictionary references, `RegimeCard` source bundles, Phase 5 validation reports and manifests must retain evaluation-only separation and exact source/configuration closure.

## 9. Vocabulary and alias lock

- Layer 4 stored actions remain exactly: `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, `unsafe`.
- `combine` may appear only as an accepted display/alias form mapped to `combine_evidence`.
- Regime, risk band/trend, recommendation, stop-loss, trust-target, trust-band and update-source values remain those already controlled by the Registry/M7 profile.
- Component names, reason details and source explanations may be structured fields but do not become canonical tokens without an accepted Registry successor.

## 10. Migration, compatibility, invalidation and rollback

1. R28 is backward compatible with R27 for unaffected content.
2. Existing artifacts remain readable under their original schema versions; no retroactive rewrite is required.
3. A newly accepted physical-schema profile creates a new schema/configuration identity and, where scientific meaning changes, a new semantic identity.
4. Accepted upstream corrections mark dependent Layer 5 derivations stale through exact source closure.
5. Regeneration creates successor artifacts and preserves supersession lineage.
6. Rollback means selecting a previously accepted immutable version, never deleting or rewriting history.
7. Future Layer 6–10 documents must pin the effective Registry revision and must not consume pending field spellings or candidate aliases as canonical.

## 11. Controlled open items

The following remain intentionally outside R28 completion:

- exact JSON/CSV/parquet field spellings and nullability rules not already canonical;
- exact interface class/API names where the Registry has not accepted one;
- formulas, thresholds, horizon values, state parameters and estimator priors;
- final repository paths and executable serialization code;
- empirical evidence and claim maturity.

These are not missing Registry decisions. They are governed downstream realization or evidence gates.

**Synchronization date:** 25 July 2026  
**Compatibility set:** `L5-R7-POST-FINALIZATION-UPSTREAM-BIDIRECTIONAL-SYNC-R1-20260725`

**Purpose:** propagate only authority-appropriate Layer 5 R7 realization details upstream and make the reverse correction/invalidation path explicit without deleting or silently rewriting predecessor content.

## 1. Authority and non-destructive supersession

The authority order remains Architecture → Canonical Registry → Execution and Evidence Plan → Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol → Phase Execution Playbook → accepted Method Selection → Nuts-and-Bolts → Implementation Build Book → execution evidence. The Layer 5 R7 document is a detailed-design realization and cannot unilaterally change a superior authority. This successor therefore distinguishes: (a) clarification already supported by the authority stack, (b) authority-specific synchronization text, (c) Registry/Protocol/Build Book/project-instance/consumer/empirical/claim matters that remain owner-gated, and (d) controlled reverse-impact packets for any future proven contradiction.

This R35 addendum supersedes only the residual Layer 5 ambiguities in R34/R28. Every predecessor byte remains preserved as the exact prefix of this successor and as a separate package member. No existing canonical family is renamed, deleted, or rewritten.

## 2. Applied canonical/profile corrections

1. `MatchedComparisonReport` is the canonical evaluation-report family. “A7 MatchedComparisonReport” is descriptive shorthand for a `MatchedComparisonReport` carrying A7 comparison/configuration identity; it is not a separate canonical family.
2. The `RegimeCard` source-lineage bundle is an **existing governed card-lineage/manifest bundle**. Layer 5 owns source preparation and lineage closure; Layer 10 consumes it read-only for rendering/export. This creates neither a new record family nor Layer 10 recomputation authority.
3. The governed boundary inventory contains ten semantic interfaces. Canonical names and normalized aliases describe one semantic object and must not be double-counted.
4. Conditional products use explicit `produced`, `empty-valid`, `inapplicable`, `blocked`, `diagnostic-only`, or `superseded` status; silent omission is invalid.
5. Physical field names, schemas, nullability, API classes, storage paths, package pins, and project-instance mappings remain Registry/Build Book owner-gated unless already accepted.

## 4. Core logical records and evaluation-only separation

`RegimeStateRecord` remains the primary Layer 5 state family and must preserve source/run/configuration/temporal identity, causal cutoff, validation/support, component evidence, RegimeRisk/state/recommendation, transition/reset/recovery evidence, trust references when applicable, stop-loss status, lineage, limitations, and diagnostic/claim tags. `TrustStateRecord` remains conditional on an independent trust lifecycle, downstream use, or claim. Runtime projections must exclude evaluation labels, current correctness, future outcomes, descendant evidence, and other oracle-only fields.

`EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, negative-control reports, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, Metric Dictionary references, and claim-evidence rows remain evaluation-only. They cannot feed training, adaptation, same-run runtime state, or hidden metric recomputation.

Normalized aliases in the R7 alias matrix are compatibility labels only. They do not create additional interface families, ownership routes, or cardinalities.

## 6. Lifecycle, promotion, correction, and rollback

All governed Layer 5 records/artifacts are append-only and source/configuration closed. Repository promotion requires schema/profile identity, exact source closure, semantic configuration hash, validation status, lifecycle/supersession state, and no stale descendant. Failed promotion leaves a run-specific artifact visible and unpromoted. Correction means append-only successor plus transitive invalidation/regeneration; rollback means selecting a prior accepted immutable version, never deleting or overwriting history.

## 7. Reverse-impact protocol

A future Layer 5 finding may not silently repair or reinterpret an upstream authority or Layers 1–4 source. It must emit a versioned reverse-impact packet containing the affected proposition, exact evidence, impacted records/interfaces/steps/gates/ablations/consumers, migration and compatibility consequences, earliest invalidated dependency, proposed owner action, and closure test. Accepted corrections create immutable successors and trigger dependency-based invalidation/regeneration from the earliest changed authority input. Rejection preserves the current authority and leaves the affected Layer 5 branch blocked, downgraded, inapplicable, or diagnostic-only as appropriate.

## 8. Owner-gated matters

| Category | Open matter | Owner | Closure evidence | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Registry-pending | physical schemas, aliases, candidate profiles/fields and BPCR dispositions | Registry owner | accepted patch/card disposition and schema tests | blocks canonical persistence only where marked |
| Protocol-pending | thresholds, horizons, tolerances, detector grids, statistical units, SESOI/equivalence/no-harm and multiplicity | Protocol v1.0 owner | frozen protocol values and analysis plan | blocks confirmatory operating point and gate sign-off |
| MetricDictionary-pending | candidate metric identities/definitions | MetricDictionary/Protocol owner | approved entries with units, direction, denominator and aggregation | blocks approved reporting of new candidates |
| Build-Book-pending | files/classes/APIs/package pins/storage/CI/cross-runtime canonicalization vectors | Implementation Build Book owner | executable implementation and integration/adapter tests | blocks implementation completion |
| Project-instance verification pending | actual records, physical fields, cadence, lateness, missingness, reset/bridge and distributions | Phase 5 execution/data owners | lawful real-artifact inspection and validation | blocks instance readiness and empirical claims |
| Consumer-readiness pending | actual Layer 4/6–10 interface profiles and consumer tests | downstream owners | round-trip and readiness acceptance | blocks downstream activation |
| Empirically unverified | A7 benefit/no-harm/equivalence/burden/recovery and real operating results | Phase 5/Protocol | immutable empirical execution under final protocol | blocks scientific confirmation |
| Claim-authority pending | thesis/clinical/deployment/real-safety claims | Layer 0 | claim review with current evidence and limitations | Layer 5 cannot authorize claims |

## 1. R36 authority, preservation and forward interpretation

The governing order remains Architecture -> Canonical Registry -> Execution and Evidence Plan -> Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol -> Phase Execution Playbook -> accepted Method Selection -> Nuts-and-Bolts -> Implementation Build Book -> execution evidence. Detailed design may reveal representational or feasibility evidence, but it cannot silently override a superior authority. Conversely, once an authority successor is accepted, every dependent detailed-design reference, configuration, artifact, interface, test, manifest and consumer handoff must explicitly rebind or be invalidated.

R36 preserves R35 and its exact R34 predecessor. R36 is the current forward Registry interpretation for the `L5-R8-POST-FINALIZATION-FULL-BIDIRECTIONAL-SYNC-R2-20260725` compatibility set. Any R7/R35 citation to R34 remains a valid historical source anchor, but canonical forward use is governed by R36. This addendum does not approve physical field spellings, serialization schemas, nullability, storage paths, APIs, package classes or project-instance mappings.

## 4. Lifecycle and promotion closure

Each required or conditional product has exactly one explicit release disposition: `produced`, `empty-valid`, `inapplicable`, `blocked`, `diagnostic-only`, or `superseded`. Promotion requires source/config/schema identity, validation, cardinality and consumer compatibility. Correction never mutates a promoted predecessor; it creates a successor, marks affected descendants stale/invalidated/superseded as appropriate, and triggers topological regeneration. Local helpers cannot be cited as canonical records merely because they are persisted.

## 5. Bidirectional Registry patch protocol

A bidirectional synchronization packet contains at minimum: packet ID and version; initiating document/version; affected proposition or decision IDs; exact evidence and source hashes; direction (`authority_to_realization` or `realization_to_authority`); impacted record/artifact/interface/step/gate/ablation/module/consumer sets; earliest invalidation root; compatibility and migration effects; owner and decision state; required regeneration order; closure tests; predecessor/successor pointers; and residual owner-gated matters. A packet cannot mark a facet complete unless the responsible owner and required evidence exist.

A Layer 5 representability finding is either: `NO_REGISTRY_CHANGE`, `CLARIFICATION_ONLY`, `PROFILE_PATCH_REQUIRED`, or `PHYSICAL_SCHEMA_OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. Until accepted, affected branches remain blocked, downgraded, inapplicable or diagnostic-only. No candidate name becomes canonical by usage frequency.

## Required packet closure states

| Order | State | Entry | Required action | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | DRAFT | finding or accepted authority change identified | identify proposition and evidence | packet complete enough for submission |
| 2 | SUBMITTED | packet has required fields | route to authorized owner | owner acknowledges receipt |
| 3 | OWNER_REVIEW | owner accepts review duty | assess authority, evidence, compatibility, impact | ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or HELD |
| 4A | ACCEPTED | owner approves proposition change/clarification | issue immutable successor and migration/invalidation decision | SUCCESSOR_ISSUED |
| 4B | REJECTED | owner rejects change | preserve authority; block/downgrade/diagnostic affected branch | CLOSED with rejection rationale |
| 4C | HELD | evidence or authority incomplete | preserve current authority and explicit pending state | OWNER_REVIEW when evidence arrives |
| 5 | SUCCESSOR_ISSUED | accepted successor exists | bind compatibility set and predecessor/successor links | INVALIDATION_APPLIED |
| 6 | INVALIDATION_APPLIED | earliest root identified | mark affected descendants stale/blocked/superseded | REGENERATION_REQUIRED or VERIFIED if no descendants |
| 7 | REGENERATION_REQUIRED | dependent artifacts require rebuild | regenerate in topological order without overwriting history | VERIFIED |
| 8 | VERIFIED | closure tests pass | record consumer acknowledgments and residual gates | CLOSED |
| 9 | CLOSED | decision, successor/invalidation, tests, and residual facets recorded | retain immutable packet and lineage | new packet only if new evidence appears |

## 4. Activation and reverse synchronization

The R3 proposals are promoted from `OWNER-READY` to `FINAL_APPLIED` at the documentary level by this resolution. The corresponding R7 reverse-synchronization rows become active for document references, logical profiles, readiness, handoffs, limitations, and open-gate status. They do **not** close a physical, numerical, implementation, empirical, consumer, or claim gate without its required evidence.

## 5. Rollback

If a later owner rejects a specific physical or numerical realization, only the affected realization/profile and its descendants are invalidated. The accepted documentary obligations and the unaffected R7 decisions/designs remain controlling. A method or algorithm may change only through an explicit controlled reopen.

| Future-layer consequence | Provides explicit contracts for Layers 9 and 10 without designing their internals |
| Limitation | Build Book implements transactions. |
| Acceptance condition | Accepted by this R42 successor at the documentary/logical-contract level; runtime readiness still requires schema/enum/foreign-key/round-trip/migration tests and the applicable Registry/Protocol/Build Book owner gates |
| Rollback | Supersede this accepted disposition through a later Registry successor; invalidate affected descendants, update the current Layer 8 successor and revalidate all consumers |


# Part III - Final R42 definition of done

R42 is documentary-complete for the finalized Layer 8 authority pair when the twenty accepted dispositions are used as the controlling logical contracts. Runtime or publication readiness remains conditional on the explicitly named physical-schema, Protocol/MetricDictionary, Build Book, project-instance, matching, held-out-stress, Layer 7, Layer 9, Layer 10 and Layer 0 gates. No controlled gate may be inferred closed from this documentary successor alone.

## Explicit non-patches

- `EmbodimentCommandRecord` is not promoted to canonical status.
- `CommandTimeline`, `EndpointErrorCurve`, `Layer9RewardTrace`, source card bundles and manifests remain governed artifacts/profiles unless the Registry owner expressly promotes them.
- No new command token, gate outcome, safety-event family, metric, reward term, stress operator or A14 is introduced.
- R42 remains controlling until an explicit R43 acceptance record exists.

## Acceptance and rollback

Acceptance requires Registry-owner review, conflict check against all R42 profiles, physical-schema/controlled-vocabulary decisions, migration tests and reverse synchronization receipt from Layer 8 R13 and Layer 9 R20. Rollback leaves R42 current and treats this patch as unaccepted proposal evidence only.

## Acceptance, compatibility and rollback

The owner must accept, reject or revise each clause individually or as an explicitly enumerated package. Partial acceptance activates only the named clauses. Every acceptance record must identify the effective version, scope, compatibility set, migration, rollback, dependent Layer 10 sections and consumer acknowledgments. Rejection leaves the controlling predecessor in force and the affected Layer 10 product blocked or downgraded.
